#197249. Tech Report: Chelsea's slump in form unpacked: The stars who badly need to step up from Emi Martinez to Cole Palmer, what defensive horror demonstrates mean for Xabi Alonso's job security - and the players in line to leave in January

Tech Report: Chelsea's slump in form unpacked: The stars who badly need to step up from Emi Martinez to Cole Palmer, what defensive horror demonstrates mean for Xabi Alonso's job security - and the players in line to leave in January

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1363 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.
  • That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.

That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.

It has led to tentative speculation around Alonso's future as Chelsea prepare to travel to Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest on Friday night, not to mention questions about where he is going wrong and how he might arrest his team's slump in form.

Here, Daily Mail Sport tackles all the burning problems at Stamford Bridge...

Chief among Chelsea’s problems is the fact they have conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. It is as many as they have scored at the other end. So, as much as we have enjoyed their freescoring forward line this season, so too must we criticise their disastrous defending.

We know Alonso can organise a defence. His Bayer Leverkusen side only conceded 24 goals when they won the Bundesliga as unbeaten champions in 2023-24. Chelsea are now on the verge of overtaking that total before we even hit December.

Liam Delap, their former striker now at Forest, will be desperate to add to that tally this Friday, too.

Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form.

Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games.

It has been revealed that this morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

Sources indicate that like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

Sources indicate that let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

Industry observers note that anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

In a recent development, believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge.

We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

He’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

Which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

Palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

It has been revealed that for me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck.

WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

Sources indicate that striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

In a recent development, we have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

According to recent reports, emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

Not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

In a recent development, alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities.

I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

As for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa intends to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.
  • The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.
  • This is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany's flagship airline Lufthansa intends to cut 1,000 jobs at its Frankfurt and Munich hubs, according to a company letter seen by German news agency DPA and news outlets.

The letter was reportedly signed by Lufthansa CEO Jens Ritter and four other board members.

This is reportedly down to ongoing financial losses. In the first nine months of the year, the airline recorded an operating loss of €180 million ($197 million).

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that the executive board noted on average the loss amounts to €20 million every month, according to media reports. The board stated in the letter that "this is the third year in a row of not being financially successful.".

"Lufthansa is currently not competitive in terms of its cost structure, efficiency and productivity," the letter said.

At the end of 2025, the Lufthansa group employed some 67,100 people, up 1% from the previous year.

The firm also aims to cut employee travel benefits, restructure its hub operations to reduce crew overnight stays abroad, and reduce short- and medium-haul capacity by replacing some A320 aircraft with A220 jets.

Furthermore, it intends to equip ten aircraft per month with Starlink, a satellite internet service developed by tech billionaire Elon Musk. The airline hopes to generate "additional revenue” by monetizing onboard internet access, according to the letter.

It has been revealed that the time frame of the cuts is unclear. It's also unknown whether the cuts were a part of a previously unveiled downsizing.

In September 2025, Lufthansa said it would slash 4,000 administrative positions due to the implementation of AI and digitalization.

In regards to this year, Lufthansa has faced rising fuel costs spurred by the US-Israeli war with Iran, further complicating its financial outlook.

Breaking: Why are Arsenal throwing away leads? Itchy trigger fingers cost Mikel Arteta's side against Dortmund

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1175 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, LONDON -- To lose one elegantly-earned lead, Mr.
  • The real impact of two points dropped tonight probably won't become clear until February and the draw for the last 16.
  • Of more immediate concern for Arteta, who was unstinting in his praise of Arsenal's "brilliant performance", is that this team's very good football is not enough to overwhelm their opposition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, LONDON -- To lose one elegantly-earned lead, Mr. Arteta, may be regarded as a misfortune; to lose two looks like carelessness. Three days after frittering away their lead at Newcastle, Arsenal repeated in the Champions League, as Borussia Dortmund became the first team to stop Mikel Arteta's side from winning a league phase game at the Emirates Stadium.

The real impact of two points dropped tonight probably won't become clear until February and the draw for the last 16. A year ago, topping the league table set Arsenal on a favorable path to the Champions League final. There are, of course, no guarantees that they would not get that as a lower seed but a repeat finish in the top two looks unlikely, with Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain both in possession of 100% records.

Of more immediate concern for Arteta, who was unstinting in his praise of Arsenal's "brilliant performance", is that this team's very good football is not enough to overwhelm their opposition. It is worth noting, at this early juncture, that this team did position itself to potentially overwhelm the German league leaders. As is so often the case with the Gunners, we're assessing them against standards that would be considered unreasonable for 99% of teams. Usually, when you put up 2.2 xG on Borussia Dortmund and give up 0.9, you can be as pleased with your side as Arteta was in public. In private, you can rest assured that he will be as detail-obsessed as this column in attempting to explain why such sustained spells of excellence still end in a share of the points.

Industry observers note that as at St. James' Park on Saturday night, for 45 minutes here, Arsenal were delicious, a true smorgasbord of footballing delights. Piero Hincapie popping up as an additional center forward, Christos Tzolis gliding off the left, Declan Rice barnstorming from third center back to second attacking midfielder in the space of a single pressing trigger.

Borussia Dortmund arrived in north London tied with their hosts for the fewest goals conceded in Europe's top five leagues. Niko Kovac's back five, with three robust midfielders ahead of them, looked like it should be enough to stifle the Gunners. Instead, they were overwhelmed, pulled here and there in their attempts to track position-lite red shirts.

Arsenal's excellence got the goal it deserved, a larruping strike from Viktor Gyokeres that moved one way, then the other, with such extravagance you rather wondered if the Australian cricket team had given the ball a going over beforehand. Nico Schlotterbeck seemed convinced he'd got an edge on it. Gregor Kobel looked dumbfounded. Even Gyokeres' belated donning of the Bane mask suggested he thought there had been some external force aiding him. Not so. You just hit it that well, Viktor.

It has been revealed that from there, Arsenal had all they needed to wrap this game up in style. Their press constricted the game into the spaces where Martin Odegaard could excel. Noni Madueke was even more menacing, a player who seems to have unlocked himself in little over a month. They kept getting into the final third. They kept getting shots, too, 14 of them before the half was out. The problem was how bad those shots were. A baker's dozen and one spare and Arsenal couldn't put up a full expected goal before the break.

Too often, moves ended prematurely because someone in red fancied taking a swing from range. Eight of their first-half shots were from outside the box. Gyokeres tried a few heat checks; come the final whistle, he was as cold as the north London night. Declan Rice has evidently read Arteta saying that he should try more shots from range. The ones from outside the box, one of which really brought the oohs as it flew over the bar, weren't even his worst. Not squaring for Madueke in the first half or Gyokeres in the second really was a spurning of prime opportunities.

If this rush to shoot from range were a one-off, you could frame it as Arteta did in his post-match press conference, "a variation in relation to the opponent, the situation that you have". And yet Arsenal have been trying from range more frequently this season, from fewer than four shots per game in 2025-26 to nearly five this term, a 23% increase in shot volume from range. Against Newcastle, the proportions were lower but twice in an excellent 45 minutes, they shot when they could have worked the ball into a better spot. Arteta has spoken about unlocking the long-range potential of his team. Those who know his thinking often frame his obsession with adding "gamechangers" to his roster in terms of players who can beat a man and strike one from deep.

They still take a lower proportion of efforts from outside the box than most teams in Europe's top five leagues but most teams in Europe's top five leagues don't employ Martin Odegaard. For now, the sample size and the variation might be so small as to be explained through happenstance or circumstances rather than design. Bukayo Saka's injury has removed one of Arsenal's primary penalty-box threats from this team. His replacement, Madueke, is still honing his shot profile, if we're being generous.

Sources indicate that there is also value to a team that faces so many low blocks proving themselves to be willing to strike from range. Fail to close down an Eberechi Eze and you might well be picking the ball out of your net soon after. Get those defenders moving out of position to close down the shot and an angle to a better opening might present itself.

It is a hard balance to strike. Tonight, Arsenal did not quite manage it: prime positions turned into subprime shots because trigger fingers got itchy.

A driving run from Joane Gadou took him away from Christos Tzolis, as the midfield busied themselves with other matters. Maximilian Beier received the ball in the box and smartly turned away from Gabriel before drilling low past Kepa Arrizabalaga. Even a defense as excellent as Arsenal's can't keep your average Premier League or Champions League opponent from clicking once. The levels are just too high.

An upswing in pressure in the final 35 minutes brought enough moments to leave Arteta baffled. "There is an element of luck here because how in hell some of the goals they haven't gone in, I don't know. Some of the days last year we hit somebody and it was an own goal.

"Quality sometimes [is missing], or [there is a] rush, or [a need] to have a bit of composure, or to read the next pass a little bit better; the execution can be better, but everything that is in between that, I think was really, really good.".

Industry observers note that he is not wrong. It just seems even more careless to let two points slip away because they could not quell their shot-first instincts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Willian has revealed how Chelsea tried to sign him months before he scored twice against them in the Champions League – and recalled the eyebrow-raising gift he received from a Blues supporter after the game.

The Brazilian winger joined Shakhtar Donetsk from Corinthians in 2007, aged just 19, but admits that he initially had reservations about moving to Ukraine.

According to recent reports, five years later, Chelsea were attempting to bring him to Stamford Bridge. Their January 2012 bid was rejected - but Willian went on to compel them to try again by scoring twice against the Blues in a dramatic 3-2 Champions League defeat that November.

Willian told FourFourTwo: "It wasn't easy. At that time, going straight to Ukraine was not my main goal. I think that every player, especially at that time, who dreamed of going to Europe, wanted to go to Italy or Spain.".

"When this offer from Shakhtar came, my family and I talked about it and thought long and hard about whether to accept it. At first, we refused.

"But they kept insisting that I should at least go there to visit the club, visit the city, and learn more about their project. I ended up agreeing.".

It has been revealed that "I spent a few days there, and I liked what I saw, including the club's structure. There were already other Brazilians playing there too. That certainly made it easier for me to accept the offer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I remember that months before that game, Chelsea had already made an offer for me.

"he game was in November and their offer came in January 2012 - but Shakhtar didn't want to let me go.".

Recent findings suggest that "So, in the end, I stayed at Shakhtar and kept trying to leave. Then, in the group stage, I ended up scoring two goals at Stamford Bridge, so it was special.

"There's something funny about that day: after the match, a fan gave me a Chelsea shirt with my name on it and a question mark in place of the number. As if to say, 'what number will he wear when he plays here?'.

"I thought it was funny and even took a photo holding that shirt!".

That supporter would eventually get their wish, in a roundabout way: Willian left Shakhtar for Anzhi Makhachkala in January 2013 before finally completing his move to Chelsea that August.

What to watch in UEFA Champions League: Manchester United face defensive crisis in tough visit to Sporting

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do.
  • Industry observers note that do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations?
  • According to recent reports, if there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, another week of Champions League football comes to a close on Wednesday night as plenty of teams on the top-eight or even top-24 bubble find themselves with work to do. A shock loss to Club Brugge means that there is pressure on Inter as they face Stuttgart at the San Siro; certainly, if they are to take up a top-eight berth, this is a game they are going to have to win.

Industry observers note that do Manchester United have such lofty aspirations? It is with the Red Devils we start, and no wonder, given their trying run of form lately. That they do have as many wins as defeats from their first four games is almost a surprise, but a difficult fixture list indicates no sign of easing for Mauricio Pochettino as his side faces Sporting in Lisbon tonight.

According to recent reports, if there was a silver lining to the very dark clouds over Manchester United on Sunday, it would have been that there is at least plenty of time to cure what ails them in the Premier League. A point from safety is a disastrous place for such an august team to be at any point in the domestic season, but when there is more than 70% of it left to play, at least the danger is not yet cataclysmic. As for the Champions League, well, United are drifting nearer to that point.

Recent findings suggest that with half their games played, they have six points. Not bad, you would have to say, good enough for 17th place in the league phase. The trouble is that their remaining four games all look difficult indeed: RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich at Old Trafford either side of Christmas, then a trip to a Villarreal outfit that should have plenty to play for on the final day. Tonight's visit to Sporting might be as good a shot at three points as Pochettino gets, and the Portuguese giants have three wins from four. He will not want to be trying to accrue four-plus points in three games.

In a recent development, it's all feeling very high stakes in league and Europe, the sort of moment when clear heads are needed. Not one for doom and gloom, or for Kobbie Mainoo to tell United's in-house channel "we're at the lowest we've ever been and no one's coming to save us." Then again, he's not wrong.

Recent findings suggest that already this club looks like it's doom-spiraling. It's on Pochettino to fix that. His first task will surely be to rustle up a defensive quartet who at least don't magnify each other's flaws. Does Matthijs de Ligt need time out to find the sharpness he so lacked against Liverpool? Can anyone fill in at left back? Diogo Dalot, still, really? Their organization will be tested against a Sporting side that attacks rapidly and centrally, qualities that should terrify a backline that will likely be shielded by the slow-moving Mainoo and Youri Tielemans.

According to recent reports, sporting always score, their 22-game streak of goals in the group stage and league phase a record for a Portuguese club. Right now it looks like United are doomed to forever concede. This could get dicey.

Recent findings suggest that in spite of what you might assume about Italian clubs, Inter's success at home and on the continent has not always been underlaid with defensive excellence. Certainly, there have been some memorable individual displays, none more so than Yann Sommer standing tall against the Barcelona onslaught, but great defense tends not to be about one player doing the spectacular over and over. After all, sometimes excellence is required because of mistakes elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that and right now mistakes are plaguing Inter across the field. Their 12 Serie A games have seen the concession of 17 goals, two in the final 10 minutes at Atalanta turning what might have been a valuable 4-2 win on the road into a chastening draw. It's the same story in the Champions League, where there have been a competition-high four errors leading to goals and another three leading to shots. Those sorts of numbers may not be very predictive, but in this case they feel indicative of a defense that has taken a step down from a level that wasn't that high to begin with.

Some of that problem lies with recruitment. It might have been time to move on from Sommer, but Josep Martinez has not proven himself to have been the ready-made replacement in the wings he might have been. Francesco Acerbi and Stefan de Vrij were similarly long in the tooth, and there was an argument for swapping out experience for experience in the form of ex-Manchester City duo Manuel Akanji and John Stones. The matter when you keep going for old guys, though, is that some of them are on the downslope (Akanji) and others can't stay fit (Stones). Being a bit too old might be an issue in midfield too.

Industry observers note that these failings are being particularly exposed in the Champions League, where Club Brugge, Real Madrid and even Shakhtar Donetsk have ended up with good shot volume and expected goals. Domestically, Inter allow a solid 1.1 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) per game, but maybe that notes more about the field in Serie A. Or maybe there's just a lot of air in four Champions League games in which 7.6 npxG has been allowed.

It has been revealed that it might be true that, as the graphic indicates, Inter's defense has stabilized a bit of late after a bad start to the season, although it probably did not feel like that when Milan were scoring three goals off 0.62 xG. It also helps no end when the attack is firing, Francesco Pio Esposito giving Cristian Chivu every manager's favorite sort of headache. However, against a Stuttgart side that can test the best defenses -- 1.96 npxG per Bundesliga game, 2.09 in the Champions League -- that defense is going to have to get its house in order.

Sources indicate that has it finally clicked for Florian Wirtz? Well, maybe. The 23-year-old leads the Premier League in chances created, trails only Declan Rice for assists provided, and is one of only five players with over two expected assists from open play this season. All that, and he ranks in the top 20 for shots and in the 91st percentile for npxG. At 11 games, it might be worth considering a few caveats. Nineteen of his 33 chances created came against Brentford and Manchester United. In the match against the former, there were an awful lot of sideways passes that resulted in long-range shots from the receiver, a chance created in law if not in spirit. As for the other game, well, it was against Manchester United. Ten-man Manchester United at that.

Wirtz can still get locked out of high-leverage games against Arsenal and Manchester City. The Wirtz who, in Bayer Leverkusen colors, seemed the surest nine-figure bet in the game tended to excel whatever the opposition. For Liverpool, it has to be just right. A game that is more up and down with fewer demands on him to break down a low block. Opponents who are slightly less muscular than the Premier League average (see Manchester United). There is still a suspicion that a league as physical and fast as England's might lessen Wirtz's effectiveness, though the man himself would contend otherwise. He says he is getting used to the demands of the league.

"I can't really say that I've changed that much," he remarked when asked how he had adapted to life with Liverpool. "I've become a bit better on a physical level and that's the only reason that could explain it.".

Credit also went to Andoni Iraola, who has afforded Wirtz a largely settled run as the primary creator in a 4-2-3-1. "He is bringing me back in a place where I was maybe two years ago where I played really good football," the German international said. "I can feel that he gives me the confidence and I'm really happy about that. I'm just trying to give him back what he gives me.".

In a recent development, expect this good form to continue in Europe, where Wirtz has generally looked a more threatening player than he does in the Premier League. In part that's a function of the aforementioned physicality. It's probably also true that the likes of LASK, Villarreal, Qarabag and Wednesday's opponents Club Brugge would not exactly be pulling up trees in the Premier League either. A chance, then, for Wirtz to build even more momentum.

One day it will have to end for Harry Kane, but for now, almost 12 years into his England life, there is still no matching the wisdom and influence he has accumulated over all those games and all those goals for his country.

According to recent reports, this would have been a great night by any measure for a man collecting his record-breaking 126th England cap. There was a handshake from Peter Shilton, now deposed as king of caps, and a flourish by Kane of his recently acquired Ballon d’Or, once his four children had accompanied him on to the pitch. These are the nights of which dreams are made, and yet – given the defining feature of Kane’s career – there was one more thing to accomplish.

According to recent reports, that was a goal from the man who has ploughed relentlessly past the two great England individual landmarks of caps and goals. His second-half penalty won the game and, although he is not infallible from the spot, he is as close to that status as England have ever had. Age has not yet run him down, he can still bend the game to his will, and when it comes to the pressure moments, his longevity seems to offer the upper hand.

In a recent development, this was always going to be Kane’s night, with a great banner on the west side of the stadium paying tribute to the England captain. The Prince of Wales was in attendance for the occasion, too. Luka Modric presented his former Tottenham Hotspur team-mate with a keepsake from the Croatian football federation. Kane had to wait for the second half for the most valuable offering of all.

After the hour, the Danish referee Morten Krogh was advised by his VAR Bastian Dankert to take a second look at a corner tangle involving Jarell Quansah, and decided to award the second-half penalty from which Kane scored. It was certainly clumsy, but these grapples have been overlooked by referees in the past. The 27th successfully converted penalty of the Kane England era followed, and the man himself played the full game.

Published: 14:56 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 15:01 EST, 25 November 2026.

Premier League officials are 'shocked and furious' after the FA overturned Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's red card at Liverpool - despite the competition's own independent panel unanimously backing the dismissal.

Sources indicate that daily Mail Sport understands that the Premier League's Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel has returned a 5-0 verdict in support of referee Sam Barrott's decision to send off Yoro. The panel also backed VAR's decision not to intervene. Their findings will be released next Wednesday.

But an extraordinary row has now erupted, with United celebrating a successful appeal while the Premier League and refereeing body Pro Ref stand by the original decision.

United appealed against the red card following Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield - Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge - and an independent FA regulatory commission, consisting of three former players, rescinded Yoro's one-match ban on Tuesday.

The Frenchman was sent off for bringing down Alexander Isak as he ran clear on goal in the eighth minute. United disputed the referee's view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens, having taken a heavy touch.

The FA panel appeared to agree, on the basis Yoro did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity, meaning the Frenchman is free to play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Referee Sam Barrott indicated Manchester United defender Leny Yoro a red card vs Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off for this foul on Alexander Isak - but his red card was overturned on Tuesday.

Barrott and his on-field officiating team from Sunday are believed to be angry at the overturn.

However, top-flight officials are now understood to be demanding answers as to how this has happened, with Pro Ref chief Howard Webb backing his referees.

Sources indicate that 'That (the red card) was the referee's call, made on the field,' said Webb. 'Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect - and formed the opinion it wasn't.

'I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving promptly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.'.

United sources have branded this interpretation as 'totally wrong' and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott's decision.

United dispute that it was a subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

The Premier League and Pro Ref did not comment.

Watch Newcastle in their current, post-Bruno Guimaraes iteration and the same problem jumps off the screen. The energy is still there, and St James’ Park can still generate an intimidating atmosphere, but unless the team go direct, things slow to a crawl when the ball reaches midfield.

It has been revealed that losing Guimaraes was always going to leave a dent in the armoury, but the extent to which Newcastle have lost their forward punch is worrying from a black-and-white perspective. And the underlying numbers confirm what supporters were worried about.

According to Gradient Sports data, Newcastle have completed the fifth-lowest number of line-breaking passes in the Premier League this season.

Guimaraes lived for disguising passes through narrow gaps, taking two or three opponents out of the game with a single touch.

Sources indicate that without him, Newcastle’s midfield is a creativity bottleneck. They right now post the lowest completion rate for 'midfield line-breaking passes' across the entire division. Instead of playing forward, the ball gets stuck under players' feet, the tempo dies, and opposition defences are given plenty of time to shuffle across and set their shape.

Not a single Newcastle player sits inside the top 38 line-breaking passers in the Premier League this campaign, as per Gradient data.

Nico Gonzalez is the closest they have, coming in at 39th. He's tidy enough on the ball and offers some progression, but the data demonstrates he is only a partial answer.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Industry observers note that gonzalez has attempted just four passes designed to break multiple lines all season, finding his man with only one of them. His numbers against the opposition's back four are similarly modest, having completed just one defensive line-breaking pass from three attempts. He keeps things ticking, but he isn't slicing teams open.

Recent findings suggest that that hesitation in the middle is costing Newcastle badly further up the pitch. In Will Osula and Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Matthias Jaissle has two forwards who are quick off the mark and desperate to stretch games by spinning in behind.

Sources indicate that both players thrive on early, vertical service into space but at the moment, they are making the runs only to watch the ball get recycled sideways back towards the centre-halves. Until someone behind them starts making those aggressive passes, Newcastle are leaving weapons unused.

In a recent development, sporting director Ross Wilson doesn't need to break the bank to sort it out this winter, either. In France, Lorient’s Arthur Avom has quietly been putting up the exact numbers Newcastle are crying out for.

Recent findings suggest that the 21-year-old Cameroon international is decisive and remarkably accurate. Compare his output directly with Newcastle's current midfielders and the difference is night and day.

In a recent development, avom has completed three out of three multiple line-breaking passes this season, alongside seven from 10 when attempting to thread balls through the opposition’s defensive line. Just as eye-catching is his overall efficiency because Avom has completed 90 per cent of his line-breaking passes so far this campaign - the same ratio managed by Barcelona's former Ballon d'Or winner, Rodri.

Granted, Avom is playing in Ligue 1, not the Premier League or LaLiga, but matching the gold standard of European holding midfielders for progression in any division is no small feat.

Avom won't cost a fortune as his contract at Lorient expires at the end of the season, putting the French club in a weak negotiating position ahead of the January window.

Sources indicate that even if Lorient hold an undisclosed option to extend his deal by a further year, a winter fee would be comfortably within reach. Guimaraes can never be replaced like-for-like, of course, but if Newcastle want their attack firing again, bringing in Avom - or a player of his ilk - is a no-brainer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Have Paris Saint-Germain been defanged? It is too soon to say if injuries have laid low the Champions League's biggest beast, but on the evidence of Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Roma, there might not be quite the same fear factor when opponents find themselves face to face with the kings of Europe's jungle.

Sources indicate that without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, both of whom are expected to miss most, if not all, of this season with knee injuries, there simply was not the final-third threat in PSG's ranks to keep Roma honest without the ball. That was all the more pronounced given that Ousmane Dembele was left on the bench until the penalty with which PSG took a 2-1 lead. Maghnes Akliouche, Senny Mayulu and Ferran Torres are talented forwards, the last good enough to win a World Cup final for Spain. Pair one or even two of them with the potential Ballon d'Or winners who started for PSG in the Champions League final, and the drop-off is not particularly significant.

Of course, it might be that Luis Enrique is not particularly minded to see how good his reserves could be flanking Dembele. It would make sense. The Frenchman's fitness needs careful managing at the best of times. With PSG having won their first four league-phase games, there was no pressing need to load up minutes on a player who will surely be needed in the spring. It was a similar story at the base of PSG's team, Ilia Zabarnyi preferred to Marquinhos, another who does well to hit a dozen games before Christmas. This might be a vision of the months ahead for an injury-addled PSG, but it might just be a team that has never taken the league phase particularly seriously not taking the league phase particularly seriously.

Whatever the longer-term view, on the field this evening, PSG's attack lacked the bite to keep Roma backing off. There is a good chance that any team managed by Gian Piero Gasperini might just go man-to-man whoever the opposition, but the fearlessness with which the Giallorossi hurtled around the Parc des Princes was a sure sign they weren't checking over their shoulder quite as much.

Instead, they felt empowered to push on, center back Mario Hermoso on hand to roll in the opener inside the box after an excellent run by Matias Soule. Again, the caveat to assessing how future opponents might take on PSG is that Hermoso has been box-crashing from defense all through this season. You can't be sure he wouldn't have been in the same spot even if he were marking Doue or Kvaratskhelia.

What you can know is that Roma's aggression when PSG had the ball in open play was not what cost them. Nuno Mendes' ability to blow by his man created issues, and Achraf Hakimi got his usual shots and shot assists from advanced positions. They could have beaten Roma, but aside from the fullbacks and a few darts into the area by Joao Neves, there was not much to scare Mile Svilar in the champions' lineup.

Instead, it was familiar failings that cost Roma, who might be a real dark horse for this competition when they can successfully defend a corner. Zabarnyi did not even have to win a duel to turn Mayulu's delivery home, just standing in the space between two white shirts at the near post. PSG's second, from the penalty spot, was a Roma confection too. Wesley could argue that Svilar should have been off his line quicker when Hakimi charged in behind, but did the Brazilian need to put his arms on his man at the exact moment he broke into the box? Wesley was lucky not to get a straight red.

It has been revealed that in such favorable positions, prime PSG often blitz their opponents. This time, even with Dembele on the field, they could not get clear. Gasperini had an ace of his own on the bench, Donyell Malen sparking Roma after his introduction. A driving run and cutback from the left had PSG scrambling, Vitinha's arm blocking a shot to hand the visitors a penalty that Malen converted.

Sources indicate that had a third goal come, it would probably have been for Roma, Hermoso blazing over late on. There was something more in this for Roma, who remain outside the top 24 despite such impressive displays against Real Madrid, Manchester United and now the holders. As for PSG, there will be time for Luis Enrique to work out how his side dominates Europe with its attack so limited. It would appear there is work to do.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that large regions of chromosomes are organized into a state known as heterochromatin. This densely packed form of DNA represses gene activity. Curiously, some families of clustered genes can be activated even though they are packed as heterochromatin. Writing in Nature, Buckley et al.1 report findings that explain this paradox: they show how opposing mechanisms that control the organization of heterochromatin promote the stochastic activation of genes in the protocadherin (Pcdh) gene cluster, thereby supporting proper nervous-system development.

With newly introduced manager Mauricio Pochettino at the wheel, however, prepares are already in motion to improve the squad – with new arrivals coming to Old Trafford in January.

Manchester United were battered at the hands of Liverpool at the weekend in Pochettino's bow, which highlighted the problems across the team.

Calvin Bassey is high on the wish list – with the Fulham man left-footed – with the likes of Jarrad Branthwaite and Nathan Collins also on the radar.

Benjamin Sesko is out until the new year with injury, with Matheus Cunha starting up front at Liverpool, while Marcus Rashford was an option to sell in the summer but remained at the request of then-manager Michael Carrick.

Ivan Toney and Folarin Balogun are options up front.

Luke Shaw will likely continue as the first-choice left-back with Pochettino having worked with the England man previously at Southampton – though with Shaw now into his 30s and with an unreliable injury record, his days at United could now be numbered.

It is believed, however, that United will not have a lot of money to spend this winter and may have to be clever with players they look to bring in.

FIFA presidential election 2027: Infantino facing Diallo and Tashima — could an alliance change everything?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027.
  • Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era.
  • According to recent reports, during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three men are vying for one of the most powerful positions in sports when delegates from more than 200 member nations of FIFA, soccer's global governing body, cast their ballots at the FIFA presidential election, to be held in Rabat on March 18, 2027. DW looks at the field of candidates.

Gianni Infantino was first elected FIFA president in February 2016, promising greater transparency and a fresh start in the wake of the corruption scandals that marked the Sepp Blatter era. Under Infantino's leadership, FIFA's revenues have continued to grow, the Club World Cup has been revamped, and the men's World Cup has been expanded to include 48 teams.

According to recent reports, during his decade in office, the 56-year-old Swiss has built a global network of support. Infantino enjoys significant backing in Africa, South America, and large parts of Asia — a result of multi-billion-dollar development programs and financial grants provided to national associations. Many smaller member associations view him as a president who takes their interests more seriously than his predecessors did.

According to recent reports, at the same time, critics accuse Infantino of consolidating power within the organization around himself. During his tenure, oversight and control bodies have been restructured multiple times, and key positions have been filled with his own loyalists.

In a recent development, infantino's ostentatious closeness to political leaders has also sparked debate — whether exemplified by his conduct during the World Cup in Qatar, his tight ties to Saudi Arabia or his public appearances alongside US President Donald Trump (though that relationship is said to have cooled significantly after the 2026 World Cup). Detractors accuse him of seeking proximity to authoritarian rulers and intermingling political interests too closely with football.

Sources indicate that A failed initiative to grant private investors a larger stake in lucrative FIFA competitions (FIFA Forward Enterprise) has also placed Infantino under considerable pressure. As the FIFA election approaches, he faces the prospect of legal challenges; European football's governing body UEFA is aiming to take action over the investment plan, while other critics are calling for an investigation by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

Recent findings suggest that however, his time in office has brought many of FIFA's 211 member associations additional development funding and other revenue. This makes him the man to beat in the March vote.

Philippe Diallo is Europe's candidate. The 63-year-old, who was elected president of the French Football Federation in 2023, is seen as an experienced sports administrator with a pragmatic and measured leadership style.

He has the backing of UEFA, as well as many of its 55 member associations, including the German Football Association (DEB).

"Philippe Diallo stands for a version of football that embraces responsibility and tackles future challenges with determination," DFB President Bernd Neuendorf said in a statement announcing the German FA's position.

It has been revealed that "We want a FIFA that serves the sport in the interest of all its member associations. That is why we support Philippe Diallo with great conviction.".

Diallo is positioning himself as a clear alternative to Infantino. His supporters see him as a candidate who stands for sound leadership, transparency, and a stronger dialogue with member associations. Unlike the incumbent, however, he lacks a global network of allies.

The third man in the race is Kozo Tashima. The 68-year-old was president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024 and has been one of the most influential officials in Asia for decades.

During a press conference in the Japanese capital Tokyo on Friday, Tashima mentioned the words "integrity, fairness, trust and transparency" several times in explaining his decision to run.

"I just don't only want to be the FIFA president, my intention is to make FIFA better," he stated.

"Being the president is the shortcut to making that happen. I just want to clean up the federation and make it a fair organization. I want to help rebuild the whole organization.".

Tashima also acknowledged that failing to have won the endorsement of any of the regional confederations — the Asian Football Confederation is supporting Infantino — makes him a longshot to win the election.

But he could still play a key role in the outcome. At a press conference on Tuesday, Diallo stated he intended to reach out to Tashima to "unite forces" to defeat Infantino. Tashima hasn't ruled out the notion.

"We do share some moral or ethical positions, so he's a great person to team up with," he mentioned.

"Diallo is also very strict in governance and he does have a lot of experience in management," he added.

However, Tashima also noted that he hadn't had any thoughts of withdrawing from the race.

If Infantino's challengers do manage to join forces in some way, they might just stand a chance of upsetting the highly favored incumbent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in.

There was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

Harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

Industry observers note that the defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England demonstrated on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel mentioned, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

They all had their moments. Anthony Gordon had a strong first half. Morgan Rogers was central to the two goals England scored in the 10 minutes after the break. Anderson demonstrated that he is one of the best midfielders in the world in the hour before his red card. Spain were without Rodri and in his absence his Manchester City successor was in control.

Tuchel encouraged his players to mount a ferocious press against the best first-phase passing team in the world. Brave, but it worked beautifully and for an absorbing opening 10 minutes, Spain looked all at sea. Such was the pressure, the Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón abandoned the usual build-up strategy and debuted his goal-kicks to the halfway line.

According to recent reports, even when Spain finally found their rhythm at the mid-point of the first half, England adapted. Thomas Tuchel praised England’s “statement win” that ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and secured top spot ahead of the world champions in the Nations League.

Tuchel and Declan Rice revealed they had both believed England would end Spain’s long unbeaten streak, and their confidence proved well-founded.

“This was of course a statement victory,” Tuchel noted. “I’m happy the players felt so confident. I felt it as well. I also had the same belief [that England would win]. I think we felt it from each other.

“The result followed the performance. I think it was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, in all aspects of the game.”.

Tuchel described the nature of England’s win as “the Azteca reloaded” in reference to the World Cup victory over Mexico, but felt the win in Madrid was the best of his reign as head coach.

Recent findings suggest that he stated: “Yeah [it was the best performance of his reign so far], given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. They were unbeaten in 43 games. So putting a performance out there in Madrid, in this environment, that was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

It has been revealed that “The last half an hour felt like Azteca reloaded, to be honest. Again, it was a beautiful week. The commitment to get better is on the highest level.

In a recent development, “I said it many times, I love these players and I love the mentality .We’re building something and that was the next step. It was an amazing atmosphere. I will bottle it up for sure and then unfortunately we have to wait until the quarter-final.”.

Industry observers note that “We had a fantastic result and performance in Croatia followed up by a very good performance at home against Czechia. We then got our homework done against Croatia three days ago and that’s what we always wanted.

Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

According to recent reports, this is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

According to recent reports, since that defeat, England have won four successive Nations League fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia by an aggregate score of 14-1. Spearheaded by the Ballon d’Or holder’s brilliance, England must win this evening in order to overtake Spain and top the group.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 17:09 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 18:48 EST, 25 November 2026.

Andoni Iraola tried to stifle a smirk on Tuesday when it was put to him that he had a fair chance of completing a perfect week by thrashing Manchester United, winning away in Europe and then winning his first-ever Merseyside Derby.

The usual responses came back of remaining level-headed and not getting carried away, of course – but Iraola has ticked off two of those three tasks and now goes to Everton with his much-criticised, substantial-money signings in the form of their Liverpool careers.

That is Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, of course, who both scored here to further quash any narratives over them being expensive flops, a debate which had followed them for much of their first year or so on Merseyside.

Isak scored a brace to take his season tally to double-figures and make it six away games in a row where he has struck, while Wirtz followed up his best performance of the season against United with a fine strike from distance.

Wirtz especially has never been far away from criticism during his time at the club but is silencing his doubters every week and said this week that Iraola had helped him rediscover the player Liverpool thought they were buying for £116million two summers ago.

Sources indicate that the sentiment spreads beyond Wirtz. After a season of strife, Iraola has brought the feel-good factor back at Anfield and supporters are enjoying watching their team again after a year in which it felt like a chore to do so some weeks.

Alexander Isak scored twice as Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League.

That made it three wins in a row for the Reds as they start to really click under Andoni Iraola.

CLUB BRUGGE (4-3-3): Sommer 4; Sabbe 5 (Siquet 84), Spileers 5, Mechele 6, Seys 6; Vetlesen 6 (Vermant 75), Potts 7 (Tsawa 84), Vanaken 6; Forbs 7, Tresoldi 6, Lemarechal 7 (Diakhon 75).

Subs not used: Jackers, Vanden Driessche, Han-beom Lee, Virgili, Dams, Robberechts, Audoor, Vasovic.

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1): Alisson 7; Frimpong 6 (Van Dijk 73, 6), Araujo 6, Jacquet 7, Kerkez 6; Nyoni 7 (Mac Allister 73, 6), Szoboszlai 7; Munoz 6 (Ngumoha 42, 6), Wirtz 7, Barcola 6 (Chambers 86); ISAK 8 (Koumas 86).

Subs not used: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Tsimikas, McConnell, Danns.

Scorers: Isak 13, 82, Wirtz 79.

Referee: Alejandro Hernandez (Esp) 6.

It is making the Liverpool fans fall for Iraola a little bit more each week. How that feeling would be turbocharged with Derby delight at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Sunday.

It has been revealed that ‘I was very pleased with the result and the performance overall,’ noted Iraola. ‘At 3-0, you can think it was an easy game and I don’t think it was. We were facing a really good team.’.

As the 1,000 or so travelling Kop enjoyed their strong Belgian beers and chocolate waffles in this quaint, picturesque city, they were still laughing about poor old Manchester United and Sunday’s 4-0 demolition job.

This was a much tougher test against an opposition that had started well in the Champions League with three wins from four, so Liverpool’s performance was never going to be as convincing – but the victory was still important.

It helped them take a step closer to cementing a top eight place in this long-winded league phase. That would ease the pressure on a congested calendar by seeing them not only be able to rest players in the latter games of the league stage but also skip a play-off round.

Club Brugge are no mugs and they showed that, with energetic winger Carlos Forbs the pick of the bunch. The former Manchester City academy starlet has inherited a certain Cristiano Ronaldo’s No 7 shirt at Portugal and gave Milos Kerkez a testing night here.

The Belgian side, like Liverpool, had won three of their first four European games including victory away to Inter. They had won five of the last seven league titles with a brave playing style that Iraola admitted was a pleasure to analyse – which he added was not always the case.

It has been revealed that their bold approach was their undoing here, though, with possession tossed away far too easily for Liverpool’s opener after 13 minutes. Yann Sommer, in the winter of his career at 37, passed straight to Bradley Barcola who, via stand-in skipper Dominik Szoboszlai, found Isak.

The Swede needed no second invitation to fire home his ninth goal of the season. Isak had been rested for most of Liverpool’s early European outings but was the difference here and loves playing away: he has now netted on his last six games away from Anfield.

Liverpool have 12 points from five games and will almost certainly be in the knockout stages.

Florian Wirtz continued his fine form as he curled in a delightful effort to put Liverpool 2-0 up.

Iraola will hope to make it the perfect week with victory in Sunday's Merseyside Derby.

Only Mohamed Salah has done so in seven or more in recent history for Liverpool. Everton would be a fine place to match that record.

In a recent development, despite the scoreline flattering Liverpool, things were far from easy after Isak’s opener. Alisson was needed to deny Felix Lemarechal both sides at half-time and Virgil van Dijk – rested from the start – was called on as a second-half substitute to steady the ship.

Recent findings suggest that winger Victor Munoz limped off in agony after going down before half-time holding his knee. Iraola feared the worst when a stretcher was called but the Spaniard walked off and was feeling ‘optimistic’ after the match, according to the boss.

Szoboszlai should have put the game to bed after a sublime team move led to the Hungarian being thwarted by Sommer at point-blank range, while Barcola was also guilty of wastefulness after getting his feet tangled up when in a dangerous position.

But Wirtz, in the best form of his Liverpool career, made it three goals in his last three with a fine strike from distance that clipped in off the post.

Industry observers note that then Isak raced through on goal and dinked a shot over Sommer for goal No 10 of the season for him. It completed a memorable night for Iraola and his substantial-money boys. Now to make it a perfect week at Everton on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has barely unpacked his bags at Old Trafford, but it's already abundantly clear Manchester United need to back their fresh head coach in January.

Following a disappointing start to the campaign and the arrival of a new regulatory era in English football, the club’s latest financial results offer a clear picture as to how much room INEOS actually have to manoeuvre.

Man United’s most recent full-year accounts, covering the 12-month period to 30 June, 2026, which were published in September, paints a picture of cost-cutting paired with historically strong commercial standing.

Despite having no European football last season, Man United posted record revenue of £677.6 million while trimming wages for a third consecutive year to £302.0m.

Although previous recruitment pushed player amortisation to £211.8m and left a net loss of £43.0m after finance costs, £47.0m in player-sale profits kept the underlying business moving forward.

Even more telling are Man United’s first-quarter results for 2026/27, released on November 19.

With Champions League football back at Old Trafford, quarterly revenue rose 4.1 per cent to £146.1m, and the club are predicted to earn £740m and £760m annually.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

Quarterly player amortisation fell by almost 15 per cent following summer exits and Casemiro’s contract expiry, while another £20.7m was banked in player-disposal profits.

This summer, the Premier League replaced Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) with its latest Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) system. Under SCR, clubs’ on-pitch spending - which comprises first-team player and head coach wages, transfer amortisation, and agent fees, while excluding non-playing staff, academy and women’s team costs - is capped at 85 per cent of football revenue plus net profit on player sales.

Industry observers note that there is even a 30 per cent multi-year buffer up to a 115 per cent ‘Red Threshold’ before points deductions apply. However, because Man United are competing in the Champions League, they must simultaneously adhere to UEFA’s stricter 70 per cent squad cost limit ahead of the March 1 compliance checkpoint.

Therefore, Pochettino has far more breathing room in the transfer market than naysayers might suggest.

Taking the £750m midpoint of Man United’s expected 2026/27 revenue and adding roughly £45m - which is an average of player-trading profits over recent years - that gives an adjusted revenue figure of £795m.

Under the Premier League’s 85 per cent threshold, Man United could carry £675.8m in annual squad costs. Under UEFA’s tighter 70 per cent ceiling, their limit sits at £556.5m.

Remove non-playing staff from total wages and Man United’s first-team player and coaching bill sits near £255m. Add £186.4m in annualised amortisation and roughly £35m in agents’ fees, and total squad costs land around £476.4m - roughly 60 per cent of adjusted revenue.

That leaves roughly £80m in annual squad-cost headroom beneath UEFA’s 70 per cent cap - and nearly £200m domestically.

Sources indicate that this means Man United could comfortably sanction £120m to £150m in winter transfer spending. That stated, their borrowing position and existing credit facility could yet prove to be a handbrake on any January rebuild, but from a purely regulatory standpoint, Man United's transfer expenditure picture is a rosy one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Just when you think you're going to settle in for a long winter's nap, there's more high-stakes women's soccer to watch. The 2026 Concacaf W Championship paves the way to the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup in Brazil and the 2028 Summer Olympics, and eight national teams from the region will play a knockout bracket starting Friday, Nov. 27.

With World Cup and Olympic berths decided along the way, fans can watch all of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship on CBS Sports Golazo Network and Paramount+.

Here's everything you need to know about the upcoming tournament:.

All times Eastern -- all games will air on Paramount+.

Sources indicate that friday, Nov. 27 (quarterfinals).

Industry observers note that saturday, Nov. 28 (quarterfinals).

In a recent development, saturday, Dec. 5 (third-place match and final).

The Concacaf W Championship is a senior women's national team championship tournament that doubles as the region's qualifier for both the World Cup and the Olympics.

This year's edition has a latest format that sends teams to the 2027 World Cup and 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The biggest change is the quarterfinal bracket. The top two ranked teams, the United States and Canada, earned byes into the tournament. Jamaica, Costa Rica, Mexico, Panama, Haiti, and El Salvador all earned spots through the Concacaf W Qualifiers.

According to recent reports, back in 2022, eight finalists were placed into two groups of four, with the top two teams in each advancing into the semifinals and clinching World Cup spots. Third-place teams were given a chance to qualify in the inter-confederation playoffs. 2022 was also the first year the competition served as both a World Cup and Olympic qualifier, but only the champion and the winner of a two-leg playoff clinched Olympic berths.

This year, the group stages are gone, and a single quarterfinal will decide who qualifies directly. In 2026, the quarterfinal winners all earn a place in the 2027 World Cup, and quarterfinal losers compete in a play-in round, with the two winners earning spots in the inter-confederation playoffs in February 2027.

The two Concacaf W Championship finalists and the third-place finisher qualify for the 2028 Summer Games. The United States are hosts of the 2028 Olympics and qualify automatically, so if they finish in the top three, the fourth-place team takes the remaining Olympic spot.

The U.S. women's national team will face El Salvador for the first time in program history. El Salvador are the USWNT's first upcoming opponent since playing Zambia in the Olympic group stage in July 2024.

Sources indicate that the USWNT step into the competition as reigning Concacaf W Championship winners. They've won the last three tournaments and hold a record nine all-time titles. The USWNT won all five of their games in the 2022 W Championship without conceding a goal and outscored opponents 13-0. The USWNT are 106W-1D-0L in matches against teams ranked outside of FIFA's Top 25, drawing only to Costa Rica 0-0 in July 2024 in Washington, D.C.

Manager Emma Hayes named a 23-player roster for the tournament, but recently made some changes following the 2026 NWSL Championship. Trinity Rodman, who sustained a shoulder injury, has been replaced by Jaedyn Shaw, and Shaw will be replaced by Lia Godfrey on the U-23 roster.

Kansas City Current defender Laney Rouse was also ruled out of the U-23 roster and is replaced by Denver Summit FC defender Natalie Means.

Recent findings suggest that el Salvador have never qualified for a Women's World Cup and will make their debut at the Concacaf W Championship. They qualified for the tournament by winning Group F with three clean sheets against Honduras, Barbados, and Trinidad & Tobago.

Head coach Eric Acuna is still leading the group after previous investigations into alleged abusive conduct,  and he publicly criticized players just last month after losses to Paraguay.

Players are trying to move forward and are led by Brenda Ceren, who led the team with five goals, followed by Danielle Fuentes with four, during the Concacaf W Qualifiers.

Newcastle are being tipped to solve their goalscoring problems this winter with a move to bring Ivan Toney back to St James’ Park.

It is a transfer which would reunite the England international with former boss Matthias Jaissle, with whom he worked at current club Al-Ahli.

Finding the back of the net has proved a major headache for Jaissle since taking the reins on Tyneside and following a summer exodus that stripped the Magpies of their spine, none of Newcastle’s current central striking options have managed to nail down a starting spot in his team.

Sources indicate that will Osula and Yoane Wissa have mustered just a single league goal apiece so far this campaign, while Matias Fernandez-Pardo is still waiting to open his account. Without a reliable penalty-box presence, Jaissle’s side have lacked a cutting edge in the final third.

Toney thrived under Jaissle during their time together in Saudi Arabia. The former Brentford frontman has been expectedly prolific in the Middle East, netting 87 times in 110 appearances across all competitions.

Any transfer negotiations may even be smoothed over by shared ownership links, as both Al-Ahli and Newcastle are majority-owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF).

Despite his form in the Saudi Pro League, Toney has slipped down the international pecking order and missed out on recent England squads, a setback that is expected to spark a push for a Premier League return in the Latest Year.

Newcastle originally signed the striker from Northampton Town over in 2015, but made just two Premier League outings before being sent out on a series of loans. Spells at Barnsley, Shrewsbury, Scunthorpe and Wigan followed, before he was eventually sold to Peterborough United in 2018.

Having since proved his top-flight pedigree at Brentford, Toney would bring additional physicality and an aptitude for finishing that Newcastle are presently missing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Legendary football commentator John Motson‘s voice is set to return to EA FC 27 through the use of AI - three years after his death.

Motson, who died aged 77 in 2023, worked on the BBC’s flagship Match of the Day programme since 1971 and covered more than 2,000 televised games, including 29 FA Cup finals and 10 World Cups.

He retired from live commentary in 2008 but continued to work on Match of the Day programme until he hung up the microphone in 2018.

EA Sports said they worked with John Motson’s family to bring back his iconic voice in a “digital tribute” through the use of fresh AI-tools, “bringing a mix of both his original audio and an AI-recreation trained by recordings of the man himself”.

The commentator featured in EA Sports’ annual FIFA game series from 1996 to 2006.

A studio spokesperson noted EA Sports have “worked with extensive care and respect to create a digital tribute to one of the game’s greatest voices, inspiring a whole new generation of football fans.”.

“My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to the team at EA SPORTS FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory in-game,” mentioned Fred Motson, son of John Motson.

“His voice inspired millions of players across generations every time they picked up a controller, and now a whole fresh set of fans will get to experience his legacy and commentary.”.

After starting as a newspaper reporter in Barnet and at the Sheffield Morning Telegraph, Motson joined the BBC in 1968 as a sports presenter on Radio 2.

His long career also took in two Olympic Games and Wimbledon’s memorable 1988 FA Cup final triumph against Liverpool at Wembley, as the Crazy Gang beat the Culture Club.

Awarded the OBE in 2001 for services to broadcasting, Motson hung up his microphone for the BBC at the end of the 2017-18 Premier League season.

EA Sports football game series began in 1994 with the release of FIFA International Soccer, with the FIFA name continuing until 2023, when the termination of EA and FIFA’s licensing agreement led to the 2024 game being called FC.

John Motson’s voice will be added to EA FC 27 in Title Upgrade v1.3.0 on 26 November as an optional commentary selection.

#197194. Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
