Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (777 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Another important opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control.
  • A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge.
  • In a recent development, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Another important opposition media outlet in Turkey has been placed under state control. On Tuesday morning, authorities raided the offices of the television broadcaster Sozcu TV and the news portal Sozcu.com.tr, and arrested several executives.

A trustee has also been appointed: The state deposit protection fund, TMSF, which usually administers the assets of insolvent companies, has been put in charge. Sozcu was one of the last big media companies in Turkey to regularly report critically on the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.

In a recent development, A large police contingent raided the broadcaster's headquarters in Istanbul, with counterterrorism officers searching the offices. According to Sozcu, its chairwoman, Funda Tuncer Sidali, and Asim Akgul, the former chief executive of the Sozcu group, were among those arrested.

According to recent reports, the broadcaster did not initially announce the appointment of the trustee on its digital channels. It did call on its audience to follow it under a new account. The leader of the main opposition party, Ozgur Ozel, declared on X: "You will never be able to prevent this nation's voice from rising, its rebellion from being heard, its cry from echoing.".

The Istanbul public prosecutor's office has confirmed the arrangements. It justified the investigation with claims of a suspected connection between the owner of Sozcu, Burak Akhay, and the Gülen movement. The Turkish government blames this movement, which was once allied to Erdogan, for the attempted coup in 2016, and has designated it a terrorist organization.

According to recent reports, according to the investigators, Akbay is noted to have used foreign bank accounts to finance two companies involved in media activities on behalf of the Gülen movement. They claim there is strong suspicion that he was able, in this way, to hold a leadership position in the organization.

It is not upcoming for the Turkish state to take over media organizations by appointing trustees. Many media companies accused of being close to the Gülen movement were brought under state control in this way after the attempted coup in 2016. What is new is that for about a year now this is also happening to media seen as pro-opposition.

According to recent reports, sozcu is not the first opposition broadcaster to be targeted by the authorities. The TELEI TV channel was searched on October 24, 2025. Its editor-in-chief, Merdan Yanardag, was arrested on charges of espionage and remains in custody. The offices of Halk TV were raided on October 14 this year. There, too, a trustee was put in charge.

In the space of just over a year, three of the most vital opposition television channels have been brought under state control. Observers see this as another step toward an increasingly authoritarian and politically isolated system.

Berk Esen, a political scientist with Sabanci University in Istanbul, sees these measures as a significant weakening of the opposition in the public domain.

In a recent development, esen told DW that the government may first have acted behind the scenes and tried to bring Sozcu to heel politically. When this didn't succeed, it invoked the judiciary. Esen notes Turkey is increasingly moving toward an authoritarian system. The attempt to prevent opposition organizations and media from gaining strength and influence is part of this.

Esen describes the opposition's success in local government elections in March 2024 as a political turning point. Since then, he indicates, the government has seen its chances of winning political competitions at the ballot box receding. "It's become harder for the AKP to win elections," says Esen. "That's why it's attacking the opposition and the free media both at once.".

Industry observers note that several opposition mayors have also been arrested in recent months and replaced by trustees. They include the mayor of Istanbul and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu, who has been in detention since his arrest in March last year. He is regarded as one of Erdogan's most promising challengers.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the Turkish Journalists' Association (TGC) spoke of a "black winter for press freedom," and unveiled its solidarity with all those affected. It described the recent developments as a serious attack on press freedom. The fact that a trustee had been appointed, first at Halk TV and now at Sozcu, indicated how the media climate in Turkey has deteriorated, it mentioned.

"These days, too, shall pass," the TGC declared. "When that day comes, those journalists who seek the truth today will be remembered, as will the decisions that prevent the public from hearing that truth.".

This article has been translated from German.

Breaking: Mauricio Pochettino is creating a siege mentality straight out of Sir Alex Ferguson's playbook - the refereeing horror show in Lisbon is just more ammunition, writes NATHAN SALT

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1309 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:10 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 02:50 EST, 26 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino's job at Manchester United is hard enough without match officials getting in his way.
  • He's got to raise the physical floor of this team, embed a high-press playing style that's at odds with the laxer approach of predecessor Michael Carrick, rid this group of individual mistakes that continue to plague the dressing room, battle against mounting injuries and suspensions, work with a modest transfer budget, navigate the press, create an identity that appears to have been lost and do it all playing every three to four days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:10 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 02:50 EST, 26 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino's job at Manchester United is hard enough without match officials getting in his way.

He's got to raise the physical floor of this team, embed a high-press playing style that's at odds with the laxer approach of predecessor Michael Carrick, rid this group of individual mistakes that continue to plague the dressing room, battle against mounting injuries and suspensions, work with a modest transfer budget, navigate the press, create an identity that appears to have been lost and do it all playing every three to four days.

But where Carrick looked eager to put out fires – part of his original appeal to bosses was his ability to steer clear of the headlines his predecessor, Ruben Amorim, brought with such frequency - Pochettino is keen to pour petrol on them and it's lit a fire that everyone inside the building is embracing. It's straight out of Sir Alex Ferguson's playbook.

Pochettino grew up idolising the greatness of Ferguson and when they shared a private lunch together in 2016, it would become a key moment in Pochettino's own managerial journey to here, now the man leading Manchester United.

In Ferguson's mind, and this was shared with Pochettino that day over lunch, he must spin two plates simultaneously to thrive at a club the size of United.

It has been revealed that the very best coaches can play a game on the pitch and one in the press. To Ferguson, winning off the pitch was as crucial as winning on it.

Mauricio Pochettino has shown in the space of a week how he can channel Sir Alex Ferguson.

A lot of what Pochettino has done thus far feels like it's straight out of idol Ferguson's playbook.

Recent findings suggest that 'Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him,' Pochettino recently noted. It highlights.

So much of what Pochettino has done so far has got Ferguson's fingerprints all over it. They were all over the pre-match interview ahead of the Sporting clash when he was asked about his start to life in Manchester.

'You've had a game as Manchester United manager now…' the interviewer began.

According to recent reports, to which Pochettino replied: 'No. I've had EIGHT minutes,' referencing the small section against Liverpool prior to Leny Yoro's unjust sending off.

Those same fingerprints were also over the club's fiercely front-footed response to ProRef following the decision for Yoro's red to be overturned. Howard Webb doubled down on the original decision, a call Pochettino and the club believed was 'totally wrong'. United are now taking up their irritation with the Premier League. Top flight referees are understood to be livid.

And then there's Lisbon, a night of total chaos, most inflicted by referee Szymon Marciniak who chalked off a legitimate goal for Amad due to a non-foul by Youri Tielemans, which he was booked for. Marciniak would later send Tielemans off having already chalked off a match-winning goal for United due to an alleged infringement by Patrick Dorgu on the goalkeeper. All of this came after he was conned into giving a penalty against Lisandro Martinez. Pochettino bounced around his technical area like Tigger, apoplectic at the unjustness of it all.

He will wait on another apology that will do nothing other than play into the siege mentality he is trying to create.

Pochettino has only been in the building a week and already he is embracing the spirit of Ferguson. Where that would lead Ferguson's United to major finals and titles, now it could be the key to Pochettino salvaging a season that has threatened to get majorly out of hand.

Pochettino's fury at decisions made against his team are protecting this fragile dressing room.

Pochettino has proven to have a firm grip on the media side so far, dictating the narratives.

He's not short of ammunition either.

His first training session, which exposed his desire to play Bryan Mbeumo out wide, use a back-three at times in possession, and have Joshua Zirkzee as a focal point, was recorded on a rogue drone that soon published its findings on YouTube. More than 100,000 views later it disappeared.

Industry observers note that then the trip to Anfield where Yoro was shown a straight red card – wrongly – for a last-man foul on Alexander Isak. An independent panel retrospectively overturned the decision 5-0, even if ProRef chief Howard Webb doubled down to back the original call.

Pochettino, armed with research, even pointed out how the opening goal from Dominik Szoboszlai should not have stood due to illegal interference with the defensive wall by Liverpool's Bradley Barcola.

Many had not even got that on the rap sheet. Pochettino cleverly planted another seed of injustice.

'Maybe the rules changed while I was in America?' Pochettino stated sarcastically.

'Why didn't they check it? It should have been disallowed. I'm here to defend my players and my club.'.

And so a furious United headed for Lisbon and were subjected to abysmal officiating that played into Pochettino's hands in terms of masking the individual errors that were as costly as the officials.

Bruno Fernandes scored a brace in Portugal on a night where Pochettino's ideas were obvious.

His demonstrative nature on touchline contrasts to Michael Carrick - and players responded.

'It's difficult to find a game where you get punished in one game,' Pochettino mentioned. 'We were punished a lot in key actions.'.

Ferguson would defend players publicly and point fingers at officials and Pochettino has so far proven to be no different.

On a night where goalkeeper Senne Lammens made two particularly costly errors, a sign of his struggles this season, Pochettino embraced him on the pitch and in the media. If anything, the defence in front of the Belgian had to shoulder the manager's blame.

Industry observers note that noussair Mazraoui, too, was culpable of really poor positioning for Sporting's opening goal, just like Matthijs de Ligt was at Anfield. In back-to-back matches, Pochettino has finished with 10 men. Each and every player got nothing but universal backing publicly.

It has been revealed that players are looking to the touchline and seeing a head coach they can respond to. Players unquestionably let down Carrick and have done their level best to drag Pochettino down in moments, too, but he's demonstrative, emotional and a totemic figure for them to rally behind.

There were signs in Lisbon of the identity that Pochettino is imprinting, signs of the high-press style, signs of a structure that has been so badly lacking, signs of a initiative, a method to lifting them off the canvas and have them back swinging punches domestically and in Europe. There were signs, too, that Pochettino and his staff have lots of work to do to flush this dressing room of the mistake culture that has crept in.

Sources indicate that by pointing fingers at the officials, Pochettino is shielding this fragile dressing room from even more scrutiny than it has already faced. Just like his managerial idol, he's proving a master of creating the siege mentality that could be the key to getting United out of the mess he's inherited them in.

'He persuaded us Manchester United are the team everyone loves to hate,' Ryan Giggs famously noted of Ferguson in 2022.

It has been revealed that 'He makes us feel everyone wants us to come second and it is us against the world. He lays down the challenge for you to take up.'.

Sources indicate that now it's Pochettino who is creating his own version. Watching his protege from the stands, no doubt Ferguson is beaming with pride.

China’s AI-powered smart-city model is going global

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that to understand the Chinese smart city, it helps to know that twenty-first-century infrastructure, technology and policy increasingly makes the whole of China a single, interconnected economic unit.
  • So, if the goal of a ‘smart city’ is to use significant data and AI to outsource governance functions, keeping everything running smoothly, then maybe we should think of China as a single city, with its different provinces and megalopolises as neighbourhoods with their own special roles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that to understand the Chinese smart city, it helps to know that twenty-first-century infrastructure, technology and policy increasingly makes the whole of China a single, interconnected economic unit. Trains, planes and autonomous vehicles shuttle about, with the centre of megacities such as Shanghai and Shenzhen merely being in the middle of ‘one-hour circles’ for commuters that allow them to reach anywhere in the wider urban area with ease. Previous barriers to the internal movement of workers, such the hukou system, which restricted access to public services based on a person’s birthplace, are being removed, making it easier for people to compete for jobs across the country. And all the while, the Internet supercharges these shifts to a nationwide marketplace, backed by an ever-expanding supply of data centres. Sichuanese farmers of organic lemons now livestream from rural villages on apps such as Xiaohongshu or Douyin as they compete for city restaurateurs to buy their products.

So, if the goal of a ‘smart city’ is to use significant data and AI to outsource governance functions, keeping everything running smoothly, then maybe we should think of China as a single city, with its different provinces and megalopolises as neighbourhoods with their own special roles. For instance, three of China’s megacities each have their own key function: Beijing regulates and invests in fundamental research; Shanghai is home to multinational corporations, frontier research in AI and biotech, and finance; and the Greater Bay Area, including Shenzhen and Guangzhou, is home to innovative manufacturers, such as electric vehicle producer BYD, tech giant Huawei and consumer electronics firm DJI.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

According to recent reports, china’s 15th five-year initiative unveiled earlier this year sees the country in this way, too, by entrusting certain functions to different cities and regions, and with rural areas also playing an essential role. In the northeast, farming is increasingly carried out with the use of drones and big data by state-owned companies such as Beidahuang. In Inner Mongolia and Xinjiang, data centres are powered by abundant solar and wind energy, where they calculate how the self-driving cars of China’s eastern seaboard should navigate roads or process the AI that helps to keep the country’s state-of-the-art high-speed train network running on time.

Recent findings suggest that this approach on data is embodied by 东数西算 (roughly translated as ‘east data, west compute’), a national-level strategic project to channel data from developed eastern regions to resource-rich western regions for processing and storage using eight data-centre ‘hubs’ located across the country. Eastern megacities generate the vast majority of China’s data and AI requests, but they bring skyrocketing land costs, power shortages and cooling difficulties that make hosting data centres unattractive. Instead, the solar farms of Xinjiang’s deserts and the wind farms of the Mongolian steppe are used to provide renewable, cheap energy to data centres.

Industry observers note that one key example is Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia, which has been transformed from a traditional farming region into a prominent data powerhouse, earning the name ‘Grassland Cloud Valley’. The energy costs in Ulanqab are low, because the government has been installing massive renewable capacity, relying on the area’s abundant wind and solar resources. Mongolia is cold for most of the year, so data centres use standard air cooling rather than massive air-conditioning set-ups — effectively, they just cover the servers with plastic and leave the door open for wintry winds to circulate. Major firms such as Huawei, Alibaba, Kuaishou and Apple have constructed large-scale cloud bases in Ulanqab. The region houses China’s largest intelligent computing centre for autonomous driving (Fuyao), built by Xpeng Motors and Alibaba Cloud, which has helped make it 170 times faster to train self-driving models. It means an autonomous taxi driving around Beijing is effectively being controlled by servers in the far-away desert of Inner Mongolia.

  • As former world champions – a title since won again – and the second-most visited country globally, Spain held the sporting pedigree and tourism capacity for huge crowds, creating a widespread expectation the final was guaranteed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

When Spain secured a joint bid for the 2030 World Cup, many automatically assumed as a certainty that the final match would take place on home turf.

As former world champions – a title since won again – and the second-most visited country globally, Spain held the sporting pedigree and tourism capacity for huge crowds, creating a widespread expectation the final was guaranteed.

Co-host Portugal had no desire for the fixture, and Spanish representatives assumed Morocco, having joined the bid late, would not fight to secure it.

In recent months, however, alarm has spread across Spain that the North African nation, a rising power in world football, might steal the tournament's biggest showpiece event.

The rivalry to host the game has evolved into a fierce clash involving Real Madrid's Bernabeu, Barcelona's Camp Nou and the $1 billion Hassan II stadium now being built near legendary Casablanca.

The contest is now tied to FIFA President Gianni Infantino's survival battle and political tensions between Spain and Morocco regarding migration.

Internal politics in Spain have also been impacted, with Alberto Núñez Feijóo, frontrunner to become prime minister following Sunday's vote, insisting Spain should drop out of hosting the tournament if denied the final.

Top-flight LaLiga chief Javier Tebas and conservative mayor of Madrid José Luis Martínez-Almeida have voiced similar concerns, with the latter admitting he "wasn't optimistic" given he saw no sign that the Spanish government was matching Morocco's ambition.

It has been revealed that inspectors from world governing body FIFA are touring host cities during this month and next, but no date has been set for choosing the location. For the 2026 World Cup final, the venue near New York was named two years beforehand.

With its team bankrolled by ⁠the state fertilizer behemoth, Morocco has united behind bringing the final to its new stadium, named after its former king, which with a 115,000-seat capacity will ​be the world's ⁠largest soccer arena.

By contrast, Spain's campaign is divided along familiar lines between Madrid and Barcelona and their two biggest clubs.

Morocco deserves the final as much as Spain, fan Bilal Jouhari, 39, mentioned in Rabat, pointing out that Morocco is fifth in FIFA's world rankings.

"Those who threaten to walk out if FIFA chooses Morocco as the final's host are just like those who abandon the game because they don't like the referee's decisions," stated Jouhari, who runs a platform promoting cultural events.

Ricardo Trade, former CEO of the ⁠FIFA World Cup Organising Committee for Brazil 2014, said Spain should have settled which city got the final as part of the original bid.

"Spain is terrified of losing the final, a final they were absolutely certain they’d be hosting," said Trade, also CEO ​for the 2016 Olympics and deputy ⁠CEO for operations at the 2022 World Cup.

"You have Barcelona on one side saying what they want, ‌and Real Madrid on the other also saying what they want, whilst Morocco seems to be very united on this World Cup project and has a stadium for 115,000 people.".

After Barcelona's president, Joan Laporta, lobbied in September for the final to go to the Camp Nou, arguing that the Bernabeu had already hosted the 1982 final, some sources in the Spanish football federation (RFEF) expressed frustration at him for undermining the unity needed to counter Morocco.

A senior Portuguese official involved in the bidding process said Spain was caught off guard, wrongly assuming that since Morocco was ‌not part of the original bid then the final was guaranteed for Spain. "They should have seen it coming," the person said.

Alvaro de Miguel, the RFEF secretary general, denied ‌there were divisions in the Spanish camp and said presenting two options against Morocco's one gave Spain better odds of success.

He noted that the bid to host the tournament was put together during a moment of instability at the Spanish FA when former president Luis Rubiales was embroiled in scandal over kissing player Jenni Hermoso on the lips at the 2023 Women's World Cup.

The atmosphere at the RFEF at the time "was not the most conducive to a project of this scale, involving a range of complex interests," he said.

It also coincided with a testy time between Spain and Morocco over migration, including a 2021 attempt by thousands of people to enter Spain's African enclave of Ceuta.

Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez overruled the RFEF's looks to announce ⁠the invitation to Morocco to join the bid, insisting on delivering the message himself during a bilateral visit to Rabat in 2018, according to an RFEF source.

His government was heavily involved in the creation of the bid and the RFEF ended up agreeing to a request from the government and FIFA to include Casablanca as an option for the final, according to three RFEF sources.

Sanchez's office declined to comment.

FIFA's Infantino has been locked in a power struggle with UEFA since Europe's governing football body demanded he step down over his strategy to sell a 20% stake in the World Cup.

Tebas remarked Infantino would favour Morocco because it was backing his reelection bid. "If Infantino stays on, Spain’s chances of getting that final are negligible or non-existent," Tebas said in September.

Morocco's football association has been one of his staunchest supporters and Infantino has spent long periods at FIFA's newly opened regional headquarters in Rabat since the selloff plan was revealed. Infantino is the favourite to win reelection at FIFA's March congress – in Morocco.

However, Real Madrid President Florentino Perez, who has a close relationship with Infantino, could help persuade him to choose Spain for the final, a LaLiga source stated.

De Miguel said the fact that FIFA's governance was under such scrutiny played in Spain's favour, since he expected it to be awarded to the "natural" candidate.

FIFA stated in a statement it has no standard procedure for selecting the venue and that the decision would follow consultations with ‌host cities, countries and governments.

Spanish officials say Madrid has experience in handling high-octane matches such as the 2018 final of South America's Copa Libertadores between River Plate and Boca Juniors, switched there due to fan violence.

They also point to the debacle in ​Rabat during the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final, when Senegal's coach ordered his players off the pitch over a penalty awarded to Morocco, footballers fought each other, and the ball boys stole the Senegal goalkeeper's equipment.

De Miguel remarked that if size ‌is a factor, then the Camp Nou will hold 105,000 by the 2028-2029 season after a $2 billion refurbishment, compared to the ⁠Bernabeu's 84,000 after its $1.5 billion makeover.

Moroccan FA President Fouzi Lekjaa said construction of the Hassan II will be completed in early 2028. According to the IMF, Morocco plans to spend about $19 billion between 2024 and 2030 building airports, stadiums, hotels and a high-speed ⁠rail network, as well as a train station and highway to connect the stadium with Casablanca 45 km (28 miles) away.

Casablanca will need to work on its hotels to compete with Madrid and Barcelona after a FIFA technical report rated its accommodation offering for the general public at 3.1 compared to 5 for Spain.

Sources indicate that but a successful bid is not just about who has ‌the best stadium, hotels and transport. Often bids go to the country that would ​receive the greater benefit, Trade said.

According to recent reports, in Morocco, the World Cup was an opportunity to expand railways and develop the whole Casablanca area, Lekjaa told state ‌broadcaster 2M. A Moroccan source familiar with the discussions noted the final should go to the stadium with the largest ​capacity — and to an African country.

"It would be awkward – embarrassing, even – and would send the wrong message to Africa, one of the world's biggest producers of raw football talent, if the World Cup final were ultimately awarded to a non-African country with a smaller stadium," the person stated.

Alonso heckled as Chelsea are humiliated by Leeds

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4029 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers.
  • Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.
  • It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are two non-negotiables for Chelsea managers. Do not lose at home to Tottenham Hotspur and do not lose at home to Leeds United. But Xabi Alonso has now completed the nightmare double.

Just as Spurs broke their Stamford Bridge hoodoo a few weeks ago, Leeds secured their first win at Chelsea since 1999 by humiliating the hosts after falling a goal behind.

It was 67 long years since Chelsea had last lost at home to Tottenham and Leeds in the same season, and Alonso was left in no doubt about how seriously supporters take that as his team were loudly booed and he was heckled.

Cole Palmer stormed down the tunnel at full time, ignoring the advice of Chelsea’s so-called “cultural architect” Willie Isa to applaud the remaining home fans, and shrugging off the attention of injured striker João Pedro.

Having been left out of the last England squad, Palmer was largely anonymous for Chelsea but he was not alone and Alonso is already facing similar questions to his predecessors about the team’s mentality.

Industry observers note that “I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment, mentally,” Alonso mentioned. “When we receive a punch, we didn’t recover that strong, that tough enough and today that was my feeling.

In a recent development, “The fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. For sure, it’s not the easiest moment. It’s a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together because there is still a long way to go.”.

Alonso is yet to name the same starting XI for successive league games and there appears to be no discernible plan or style of play.

Injuries have contributed to Chelsea’s unremarkable start to the season under Alonso – and Moisés Caicedo was forced off early in the first half – but the problems run deeper than the treatment table.

Alonso’s defence has now conceded 20 goals, which has contributed to Chelsea losing five league games already – more than Manchester United. In between three defeats in their last four league games, Chelsea were also knocked out of the Carabao Cup.

The Spaniard had answered questions about Chelsea’s identity, or lack of it, by saying he wanted his team to be competitive. But they were anything but against a Leeds side who had seven more shots than their hosts and five more on target.

Sources indicate that it is hard to fathom how, through all the chopping and changing, Wesley Fofana still starts games for Chelsea in defence. It was his pathetic attempted header, which bounced backwards towards his own goal, that contributed to Noah Okafor’s first goal.

Josh Acheampong also got himself into a mess and Okafor was somehow able to squeeze a shot past goalkeeper Emi Martínez despite having three Chelsea players around him.

Chelsea had taken the lead through striker Emmanuel Emegha, on his first start for the club, but from that moment on they were second best with Leeds pair Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka running the middle of the park.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin had hit the crossbar and failed to find the net with three more presentable opportunities in the first half, but he took his chance from the penalty spot eight minutes after the break.

Morgan Rogers had argued that James Justin’s shot hit him too far up his arm for it to be a penalty, but a VAR check upheld referee Michael Oliver’s decision and Calvert-Lewin kept his cool.

That should have been the moment that shook Chelsea into action and prompted a response but, instead, Alonso’s team fell apart and he was unable to provoke a shift in momentum from the touchline.

Just five minutes after Calvert-Lewin had put Leeds ahead, Okafor effectively sealed the victory by firing the ball into the net after Chelsea had failed to deal with a long throw into their penalty area.

Noah Okafor's brace helps seal Leeds' first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge since 1999! 💥 https://t.co/UAmsJziJmZ.

Sources indicate that “I can’t wait to be on the sofa with coffee and cake and also watch this game back because it was a really good game,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds head coach, stated. “I was a bit disappointed even at half-time when it was just a draw, because I think we were the better side from the first to the last.”.

It has been revealed that john Terry still works with Chelsea’s academy and it might be worth Alonso getting the former captain to speak to the club’s senior players about how to defend and compete. Whatever has been done on the training pitch so far has not worked.

Recent findings suggest that alonso’s substitutes are yet to register a single goal or assist in the league this season and his changes failed to make any sort of impact here. For the visitors, however, two substitutes combined to score their fourth goal in time added on for stoppages.

Harry Wilson played in Brenden Aaronson and, from a tight angle, he managed to find the back of the net by sending the ball through the legs of Martínez.

The home stands were already half-empty by that point, but some supporters hung around to show their displeasure and Palmer could not contain his anger.

Sources indicate that we know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It’s right we can enjoy this performance.

Frank’s start to life at Palace begins with defeat but an improved display. Coventry are up to 13th with their fourth win of the season.

Another home win for Tottenham, who managed the game well and introduced a new star to the Premier League in Williams-Barnett.

In a recent development, what a day for Leeds. They scored four and it could have been more. For Chelsea, they lost their way when Caicedo went off and without Joao Pedro, they have lost their spark in attack.

Bournemouth make it nine wins in a row in all competitions after doing enough in the first half to get the job done.

Leeds finish the match in style as Aaronson puts the seal on an impressive away day.

Industry observers note that it’s all over and Sunderland deservedly leave with a point. Villa will be very disappointed by their display.

In a recent development, what was I saying in the last post?! The home side are on the attack Thomas-Asante pokes a shot at goal and forces Henderson into a save but hits his own player McNeil, who bundles the ball in the net.

It has been revealed that can Chelsea stage a late fightback? Will we get a winner between Coventry and Palace?

Needing a goal, Emery makes a bold decision to take off Villa’s top scorer and bring on Madjo.

Despite the two-goal lead and the magnificent debut performance of Luca Williams-Barnett, the home support has remained subdued throughout the afternoon.

At times, the shouts of two children sat just behind the press box feel like by far the loudest noise in the stadium - although that might just be proximity.

Much quieter half at the CBS Arena but Palace are more likely to get a third goal.

This has gone from bad to worse for Chelsea. One supporter near the dug-outs was so angry at Leeds scoring a third goal that he got up and screamed his displeasure at manager Xabi Alonso.

Recent findings suggest that 1999 was the last time Leeds won at Chelsea. Today looks like they will get another, as Okafor takes advantage of more poor defending to finish past Martinez.

Villa’s fans are now chanting loudly for substitute John McGinn to be introduced.

They are getting their wish, too, as the Scotland international is coming on with winger Ibrahim Mbaye.

Villa need an injection of energy.

It has been revealed that morgan Rogers and Chelsea are pretty upset about that penalty being awarded to Leeds. They felt the ball struck him too far up his arm to be a penalty. Calvert-Lewin took his spot-kick superbly and it’s gone very, very quiet among the home fans.

Everything Luca Williams-Barnett touches is turning to gold today. He has a goal to his name already, and adds an assist just six minutes into the second half.

From almost the halfway line, he drove forward, weaving his way expertly into the box before picking out Dominic Solanke in the middle of the box, who tapped the ball into the back of the net.

However, the atmosphere is still a touch subdued, despite James Maddison urging the crowd to make themselves heard almost immediately after the goal, the noise drops to almost a murmur.

Sources indicate that rogers blocks Bogle’s drive with his arm and Michael Oliver gives a penalty to Leeds. After a long check, VAR confirms it.

Calvert-Lewin steps up and sends Martinez the wrong way. The away team deserves this. They have been the better side. That is Calvert-Lewin’s 100th club career goal.

Williams-Barnet gets one-on-one with Furlong and gets past him with ease before firing a cross for Solanke to finish.

The whistle blows for the second half around the grounds. What will the second 45 minutes have for us?

A real lack of quality here from both teams, and Sunderland deserve credit for weathering the early pressure.

Villa appear short of creativity and have managed only one shot on target in the first-half.

Sunderland have defended resolutely and caused Villa’s back-four some problems in the rare moments they have attacked.

Unai Emery marched into the dressing room after the half-time whistle and has much to ponder.

Some boos from the Chelsea fans at half-time. Calvert-Lewin could have had a hat-trick in that first half, sending one header against the bar, two too close to Martinez and flicking a shot just wide. Leeds also had a goal ruled out for offside.

Chelsea just stopped playing after taking the lead.

According to recent reports, that half was all about Luca Williams-Barnett. The 18-year-old scored in his first start, and had two opportunities to add to his tally just before the break. He had a header tipped over the bar by Christian Walton and a chance from close range stopped on the line. The future looks bright, as they say.

However, Tottenham faded after a strong opening 15 minutes, and Ipswich were able to break up play and get forward more, exploiting the home side’s lack of a defensive midfielder, and that will be something for Roberto De Zerbi to address in the break.

Recent findings suggest that we have whistles around the ground. That was breathless stuff.

The visitors will feel they should be in front at the break. First, Muharemovic thinks he has scored when he head in a cross from Justin but he was offside.

Then Ampadu’s long throw finds Calvert-Lewin in space and his shot is saved by Martinez. Should have done better there.

Bournemouth finish the half in style. Kluivert gets the second when he taps in a cross from Tavernier.

Palace hit back again. Pino clips a cross to Larsen at the far post and he heads past Rushworth coolly.

Courtesy of Opta: Aged 18 years and 51 days, Luca Williams-Barnett is Tottenham Hotspur’s youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale against Fulham in September 2007 (18y 47d).

Villa are in desperate need of a spark and one has to wonder when John McGinn will be introduced. McGinn is on the bench today and the home team are crying out for some inspiration.

Villa did start brilliantly, yet the game has now petered out into a mess of misplaced passes and poor decision-making.

According to recent reports, still no clean sheet for Emi Martinez. But Noah Okafor’s goal wasn’t his fault – he was let down by some bad defending from Wesley Fofana and Josh Acheampong.

Martinez did start Chelsea’s 2-0 victory over Everton, but he didn’t last the full game as he had to be replaced because of injury.

A touch of Hollywood royalty in attendance at Tottenham on this cold November afternoon with Sir Kenneth Branagh and Ryan Reynolds in attendance.

Reynolds is a co-owner of Wrexham, who are at the moment playing in the Championship at Lincoln City, but he has chosen to watch football in north London instead.

Sakamoto puts Palace back in front with a brilliant finish. Rudoni gets away from Khalaili and crosses to the Japan international. Sakamoto brings it down nicely then rifles a shot into the top corner.

It has been revealed that that lead did not last long for Chelsea. The away side hit back within three minutes as Okafor shoots through the legs of Colwill and into the net.

Another full debutant and another goal. This time at Stamford Bridge as Emegha latches onto a ball from Rogers and blasts an unstoppable shot from distance.

Emegha had to wait a while to make his first start for Chelsea, but he’s marked it with a really well taken goal. Leeds will be disappointed with the time and space he and Morgan Rogers, who provided the assist, were given, but it was a good finish.

Caicedo just can’t get going this season. That back injury that forced him off the pitch for a minute earlier has now resulted in him having to be replaced by Jordan Henderson. That’s a real blow to Alonso and Chelsea.

Villa were completely dominant in the opening ten minutes but Sunderland have now managed to subdue the home team.

Johan Manzambi and Nicolas Jackson are both impressing for the home team. Villa do appear a little vulnerable in defence when Sunderland do break forward.

Today will be a day that 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett will not forget in a hurry, he has been energetic since the start and marked his maiden Premier League start with an early goal.

The actual goal might have been a tap-in, but it has injected life into the crowd who had otherwise been largely subdued from the start.

Recent findings suggest that confusion on the touchline for Chelsea. Caicedo was down after hurting his back. Alonso tried to stop his phyisos going straight on to the pitch, but referee Michael Oliver called them on. That meant Caicedo had to spend a minute off the pitch under the latest rules.

According to recent reports, remember this moment because on his first senior start Williams-Barnet has made it a special one with goal. It was scrappy but he will not care. The Tottenham fans have been talking about his young fan for a long time.

Sources indicate that equaliser for Palace and Frank. Very good response from his players as Larsen flicks the ball to Pino and the Spain international fires into the net.

No shots on target from either side but it is already shaping up to be attack vs defence. Villa are dominating the goal and looking threatening.

Awoniyi is through one-on-one with Henderson, goes around the keeper but Disasi does brilliantly to recover and make the block.

Worst possible start for Frank and Palace as Awoniyi gets his second goal of the season with a cool finish.

A video of De Zerbi saying “let’s go” in a manner that might be more at home in American Football is shown before the teams come out onto the pitch.

The atmosphere feels a bit subdued so far, but it is an notable match for Tottenham.

We are underway around the grounds!

This is probably the kiss of death from me, but I’m really looking forward to watching Tarik Muharemovic today. The defender has impressed me every time I’ve watched Leeds on television this season and looks to be one of the signings of the summer. Dare I say it, but Chelsea could have done worse than sign him given their troubles at the back. Emi Martinez is back in goal for the home side. He’s yet to keep a clean sheet since signing from Aston Villa.

Thomas Frank declared “it’s good to be back in the circus” of football management ahead of his first match as Crystal Palace boss.

The 53-year-old Dane admitted he could have easily spent a few more months sipping wine, “eating too well” and collecting passport stamps, but something resonated when he asked his wife why he was tempted to seek out a new job and she told him, “(It’s) because you can’t help yourself”.

Frank hinted that there was more behind the story to his disappointing spell at Tottenham he might one day reveal, but for now he has a team to rescue from a relegation fight, beginning with today’s trip to Coventry.

If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better.

In a recent development, of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. The details, that will be for another time, but I can say I’ve learned, definitely.

Recent findings suggest that I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time. I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.

I was spending time with family and friends and doing all that, but I think the club, the way Palace is, how well Steve Parish especially spoke about the club and ideas, Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody and these guys, too, helped convince me it was a good idea.

Construction news: work on the North Stand behind one of the Villa Park goals continues to progress.

There are clear structural changes since Villa’s last home game and a mural of fans makes it more appealing to look at.

This stand is scheduled to be ready for next season and will increase Villa’s capacity to over 50,000.

Tottenham’s impressive run of form came to a crashing halt with a 1-0 defeat to Leeds just before the international break, but manager Roberto De Zerbi will be hoping for a fresh start - even if he will not be pitchside after picking up a second yellow card of the season.

De Zerbi made six changes from the aforementioned defeat to Leeds, including a first start for teenager Luca Williams-Barnett, a player who has come through the club’s academy.

There is no place in the squad for Sandro Tonali or Tosin Adarabioyo, but James Maddison will start for the first time since the 2-0 defeat to Chelsea in October.

Aston Villa 2.0 was always likely to be a slow-burner, and it is proving exactly that for Unai Emery.

His team has impressed and underwhelmed in equal measure so far this season but this is an opportunity to hoist themselves up the table.

A clean sheet would be a good starting point, as they have not secured a shutout in front of their own fans in the league since March.

There is no Alejandro Garnacho or Tammy Abraham in the matchday squad today.

Good afternoon and welcome to coverage from the Premier League as domestic football returns after an international break.

We have five matches to bring you, including Chelsea vs Leeds, Aston Villa vs Sunderland and Tottenham vs Ipswich.

Xabi Alonso noted his Chelsea side needs to learn to deal with the absence of Joao Pedro as the Blues struggle for goals in the absence of their injured striker.

The Brazilian has not played since the 2-0 win over Everton on October 17 and will be unavailable again today.

Without a focal point in the number nine position, Chelsea’s goal output has been dramatically reduced and they have dropped to fifth and having suffered two defeats in their last three games.

Industry observers note that “(We need) the whole team for that,” said Alonso. “It’s not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.

Sources indicate that “It’s teamwork. For sure Joao is an notable player but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.

According to recent reports, “We need to deal with it. It’s not that I’m going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.”.

Tottenham will not have their manager, Roberto De Zerbi, on the touchline after receiving three yellow cards this season.

Gary O’Neil is targeting a “special” result at Tottenham, but promised Ipswich will not make any drastic changes after a four-match winless run.

Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the two-week break, which followed draws with Hull and Nottingham Forest along with a narrow defeat at Manchester City, but O’Neil is happy with his fresh-look group.

“There won’t be any drastic changes. The odd personnel change, (but) I don’t think it’s going to be a massive shift for us,” O’Neil told a press conference.

It has been revealed that “It’s a very well-balanced squad. There’s going to be no massive uplifts or downgrades when we have to change players within this group.”.

Aston Villa will have Johan Manzambi available for the visit of Sunderland.

The midfielder did not feature for Switzerland during the recent international break because of a calf injury but he has trained with the rest of the squad and can feature today.

Recent findings suggest that villa can also call on right-back Aaron Wan-Bissaka after a muscle injury ruled him out for six matches. His return is timely as Matty Cash is unavailable.

Cash was suspended for Villa’s 4-4 draw with Manchester United before the international break but suffered a concussion while away with Poland.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sunday’s bruising 4-0 defeat at Anfield exposed the scale of the rebuild facing Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United.
  • For all the scrutiny aimed at Man United’s midfield and attack, it is the fragility at the back that is of greatest concern - the club have now conceded more goals than any other side in Europe's top five leagues this season.
  • With the January transfer window fast approaching, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey - often linked with an Old Trafford move - is rapidly playing himself into contention for a switch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sunday’s bruising 4-0 defeat at Anfield exposed the scale of the rebuild facing Mauricio Pochettino at Manchester United.

For all the scrutiny aimed at Man United’s midfield and attack, it is the fragility at the back that is of greatest concern - the club have now conceded more goals than any other side in Europe's top five leagues this season.

With the January transfer window fast approaching, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey - often linked with an Old Trafford move - is rapidly playing himself into contention for a switch.

Man United’s need for centre-half reinforcements could hardly be more urgent after the weekend's display. Matthijs de Ligt looked worryingly off the pace against Liverpool, struggling with his turning circle and repeatedly caught out whenever Andoni Iraola's side broke at speed.

The long-term picture looks increasingly bleak, too. Lisandro Martinez is widely expected to move on at the end of the season after previously speaking out publicly against the club, leaving a left-footed vacancy at the heart of defence.

In a recent development, across the rest of Pochettino’s central defensive options, there is a lack of ready-made solutions. Leny Yoro, who endured a miserable afternoon of his own on Merseyside, and Ayden Heaven are both still very junior in their development, while Harry Maguire isn't getting any younger.

Throwing teenagers and early-20-somethings into an Old Trafford pressure cooker every week is no recipe for climbing the table, nor can Man United rely indefinitely on an ageing veteran to bail them out, as Maguire has done so consistently in the past.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

That is why Bassey ticks so many boxes for Man United’s new era under Pochettino.

Industry observers note that turning 27 on Fresh Year’s Eve, the Nigeria international is entering his prime years as a defender. And having racked up more than 100 Premier League appearances since arriving in west London from Ajax in 2023, he brings the sort of battle-hardened top-flight pedigree Man United are crying out for.

In doing so, he removes the adaptation risk that has plagued so many overseas Old Trafford arrivals. His commanding display in Fulham’s 1-1 draw away at Manchester City on Saturday makes the appeal obvious; Bassey has good recovery pace, is dominant in physical duels, and comfortable defending wide channels.

Bassey won't cost the earth either as his initial four-year contract at Craven Cottage expires next summer, and although Fulham hold an option to extend his stay by a further 12 months, his contractual situation keeps any potential fee firmly within reach for a club of Man United's stature and commercial acumen.

Fulham are understandably eager to tie him down to fresh terms, but the lure of spearheading Pochettino’s Old Trafford reboot may prove hard to resist.

In FourFourTwo's view, if Bassey maintains his current level over the coming weeks, don't rule out a January approach.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

European Union top officials and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced deals on trade and youth mobility at Friday's Brussels summit.

This might be the first step to rebuild ties, a decade after Britain voted to leave the EU.

During the delegations' meeting, Burnham said the deal was a "landmark agreement," while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called it a "turning point" in relations.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is a good day for Britain. This is a good day for Europe," Burnham remarked.

Speaking at the joint press conference, European Council President Antonio Costa said the bloc respected the British decision to leave the EU and would respect its choice to strengthen ties in the post-Brexit era.

He mentioned jokingly that the EU and UK "may drive on the opposite sides of the road, but what matters is they are heading for the same direction.".

Burnham said that the deals were made with young people in mind, adding: "This deal is for you. This deal really is about lifting your life chances.".

He went further and stated "Brexit took opportunities from young people," and that they have to "open up new opportunities" for young people.

Von der Leyen remarked the youth experience project would "open horizons and create friendships that will last a lifetime.".

She said the trade agreement is a "two way street" and it means "more choice for the customers.".

Von der Leyen also mentioned the agreement on the carbon market, saying that it would cut emissions and generate investments in cleaner industries.

She also remarked Britain will rejoin the Erasmus+ program, adding, "We miss them so much.".

Burnham said the agreements reached Friday, however, represent the most the UK could achieve at the moment, "What we are announcing today is probably ‌the limit of what we can achieve in this ‌Parliament, given what needs ‌to be done to implement it.".

In September, Burnham said he would seek a political consensus on the country's future relationship with the EU, even suggesting he could campaign to take Britain back into the bloc at the next election.

In a recent development, "Britain and Europe share values, interests and a global neighborhood. In a more dangerous world, we are stronger together. A closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe," Burnham noted as he arrived in Brussels.

The three key agreements establish ways to:.

The "youth experience scheme" would allow 100,000 people under 30 from each side to reside for up to three years in each other's territory for work, study or travel without being subject to existing visa requirements.

Industry observers note that no deal was reached on tuition fees for EU students studying in Britain, a deal-breaker for the bloc. The EU has pressed for the UK to reduce university tuition fees for EU students to the same level paid by British students.

"There will be further discussions coming out of it on problems including on tuition fees," Burnham noted.

Von der Leyen ‌mentioned ⁠she was confident negotiators would reach a ​solution ​on ‌tuition fees, "We will be working ‌on that in ‌the ​next month and as we have a ​track record of finding ⁠solutions,.".

Sources indicate that on the food deal, the EU and UK have agreed to scrap certificates and border checks on food and animal products to ease post-Brexit trade. In return, Britain will align more closely with EU food safety and animal health rules.

They also agreed to link their emissions-trading systems, allowing them to recognize each other's carbon allowances and exempt traded goods from carbon border taxes.

According to the AFP news agency, London estimates the deal could boost the British economy by 3.8 billion pounds annually, and spare 6.5 billion pounds worth of steel, aluminum and other industrial exports from additional taxation.

Leaders remarked they will establish a "structured dialogue on migration." Their joint summit statement said this would include "engagement with third countries" and "returns to third countries," among other issues.

The two sides agreed to launch formal talks on economic security and strengthen cooperation on export controls and supply chains, among other areas.

On Monday, Burnham stated it ​was the "obvious truth" that ‌Britain had lost more than it had gained from Brexit.

Polling firm YouGov runs a regular tracker on whether the UK was right or wrong to vote to quit.

Since mid-2022, a majority of people surveyed stated Britain was wrong to leave.In September, the "Bregret" camp rose to 60% — the highest ever.

Sources indicate that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

A medical tribunal has heard that a doctor who helped save the life of Premier League footballer Fabrice Muamba engaged in sexual activity with a "vulnerable" patient on practice premises during working hours.

Dr Jonathan Tobin, based at Kirkham Health Centre in Preston, was among four men who assisted Muamba when the midfielder suffered a cardiac arrest on the pitch while playing for Bolton at Tottenham in an FA Cup match in March 2012.

Muamba’s heart stopped for 78 minutes, but he was able to make a full recovery before announcing his retirement from football five months after the incident.

Mr Tobin received further praise in November 2021 when Wigan Athletic striker Charlie Wyke thanked him for saving his life following a cardiac arrest during training.

However, Mr Tobin has now been struck off the medical register after scheduling unnecessary medical appointments to meet a "vulnerable" woman and subsequently falsifying her medical records to cover up their relationship, a Medical Practitioners Tribunal panel wrote.

Recent findings suggest that the panel heard that their relationship initiated after they kissed inside his consulting room in July 2024 and persisted until November of that year. Mr Tobin admitted to engaging in sexual activity at the surgery during working hours, and acknowledged dishonestly altering her records twice to state she failed to attend appointments.

Fully aware of the woman’s vulnerability, Mr Tobin acknowledged that she needed "a good empathic GP", adding: "What she got was incredibly harmful." Stephen Brassington, his legal representative, stated that the doctor accepted complete responsibility, noting that his shame and contrition "could not be more obvious".

The tribunal observed that Mr Tobin’s professional style was "informal, friendly, and made use of humour", adding: "He enjoyed being popular with his patients, rather than being formal.".

The panel further wrote: "Dr Tobin allowed himself to form a sexual relationship with this patient in his surgery when all his professional training and experience will have told him that behaviour of that nature was unacceptable.".

Despite acknowledging that Mr Tobin had been a "fine doctor", the panel concluded that maintaining his registration would undermine public trust and confidence in the profession, issuing an immediate order of suspension.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ethan Nwaneri's Arsenal career appears to be floundering, with the on-loan Borussia Dortmund teenager facing a further transfer setback.

Nwaneri returns to his parent club tonight in the Champions League with the Bundesliga giants and is eligible to face Arsenal despite still being owned by the Gunners.

But beyond this campaign, his future remains uncertain, with manager Mikel Arteta even recently alluding to the teenager's struggles at Signal Iduna Park.

Nwaneri became the Premier League's youngest-ever player in 2022 at the age of 15 – with Max Dowman later taking that record – before establishing himself in the 2024/25 season as a serious option on the right wing for the Gunners.

But after going out on loan at Marseille last term and heading to Dortmund this time, the teenager is yet to impress, with Arteta even admitting this week that “moments are not enough” for Nwaneri in his development and that consistency must follow.

A report from Sport Witness, likewise, reads as bad news for the 19-year-old, with the Gunners now pursuing a move for Gilberto Mora as soon as January.

Mora was the youngest player selected for the 2026 World Cup and has impressed hugely in his native Mexico, courting the attention of virtually every big club in Europe.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In attacking midfield areas, Arsenal already have the likes of Martin Odegaard, Mikel Merino, Eberechi Eze and Max Dowman – with the latter two options on the wing – and should Arsenal bring in another teenage talent, Nwaneri's first-team opportunities would appear even scarcer.

FourFourTwo understands that the Gunners were open to offers for the starlet over the summer, opting to retain him and develop him at one of the best finishing schools in European football, though the paths of Nwaneri and Hale End colleague Myles Lewis-Skelly have been drastically different, thanks, in part, due to competition for places.

With Liverpool also circling for Mora, however, the Gunners may well have to present a particularly enticing package to secure the 18-year-old.

According to the report, the youngster has a release clause of around €25 million, making any move for him particularly costly – and suggesting that the Gunners could well incorporate him into their first team immediately.

In a recent development, nwaneri, meanwhile, is valued by Transfermarkt at €25m. Arsenal return to Champions League action tonight against Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Mauricio Pochettino saw his fresh Manchester United defence concede two penalties in the space of three minutes as the faced Sporting in the Champions League in Lisbon.

The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg.

If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left.

But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box.

Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row.

It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season.

United’s players were also left furious as Amad Diallo’s equaliser was disallowed for a foul in the build-up.

Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad.

Madrid's perfect home record and star quality makes it difficult to see anything other than a comfortable win for Los Blancos.

Germany, who finished top of Group A2 following their 5-0 win over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday are to face Belgium in the Nations League quarterfinals — after they finished second in Group A1. The Belgians recently came up with a statement result of their own, beating Italy 4-1. The match-up between the neighboring countries promises to be closely contested, with Belgium sitting at No. 8 in the men's rankings, three places above Germany.

The head coach of Belgium is former Bayern Munich player Mark van Bommel, who took over from Rudi Garcia following the World Cup, where they were knocked out by eventual champions Spain in the quarterfinals.

Germany head into the knockout phase on a high note, not only because they won their group, but also the way they performed in their last two matches, against Serbia and the Netherlands in the group stage.

It has been revealed that germany head coach Jürgen Klopp followed the draw, held in Nyon on Friday, from the German FA's (DFB) Frankfurt offices. He played down the notion that Germany enter the tie as the favorites.

"I've practically never given it any thought. It's never interested me," he said.

In a recent development, "An awful lot can happen in that time. We're very happy with the final impression we left, yet we're also fully aware that we're only at the very beginning of a development process. We want to carry this positive momentum forward—there's still a great deal to be done.".

The matches are slated for March 25 and March 30, 2027, and having won their group, Germany will have home-field advantage for the second leg.

Germany and Belgium have faced each other 26 times to date, with West Germany and Germany having the upper hand with 20 wins, five defeats and one draw.

Should Germany advance to the semifinals, they will go on to face the winner of England and Norway, a World Cup quarterfinals rematch.

In the other two semifinals matchups, the Netherlands drew Portugal, while the top pairing sees Spain face France in a rematch of one of last summer's World Cup semifinals.

The "Final Four" mini tournament is to be held from June 9 to 13 but the host venue won't be determined until the semifinal lineup has been completed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Manchester United were furious as Amad Diallo’s equaliser against Sporting was disallowed for a foul in the build-up.

Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad.

The United winger saw his shot saved by Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira but he followed in to head the ball into an empty net.

However, because Marciniak had already blown his whistle to stop play following the challenge from Tielemans, VAR could not intervene.

Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad.

Tielemans was also booked by Marciniak, who took charge of the 2022 World Cup final, for protesting.

Industry observers note that “It was a dreadful decision,” former United midfielder Owen Hargreaves said on TNT Sports. “I don’t know what [the referee] saw. [Tielemans] played the ball. It wasn’t reckless.”.

It came after Mauricio Pochettino saw his upcoming defence concede two penalties in the space of three minutes in a shambolic first-half spell.

The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg.

If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left.

But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box.

Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row.

It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season.

Three days after Pochettino was left raging over Leny Yoro’s early red card at Anfield, United were held to a 2-2 Champions League draw by Sporting after conceding two penalties and having two goals disallowed by Polish referee Szymon Marciniak who also sent off Youri Tielemans.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s difficult to find a game where you get punished so much in one game. We were punished a lot in key actions,’ stated Pochettino.

Asked if the decision to rule out Amad Diallo’s goal before half-time and book Tielemans was particularly harsh, the United manager remained tight-lipped but nodded.

In a recent development, ‘It’s difficult to answer because I think everyone knows it’s impossible to understand why that happened on the field,’ added Pochettino before adding sarcastically: ‘I think it's a good welcome for us after seven days! Today it's going to be my first week in charge.

‘Through our experience, if we go back and remember circumstances in different clubs, things like this you will suffer because it's the circumstance that always is against us.’.

Mauricio Pochettino gave his verdict on the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak.

Marciniak was at the centre of several controversial decisions as United drew 2-2 with Sporting.

Pochettino also defended his goalkeeper Senne Lammens who was at fault for both Sporting’s goals despite saving a penalty.

Sources indicate that ‘Football is about making mistakes,’ he said. ‘I want to support always my player. It's something that happened in that case.

It has been revealed that ‘It's our responsibility too to provide the best tools. I think in this type of action also our defensive line needs to cover better the keeper because it was very difficult.

‘It's to blame us because I think we need to manage better this type of situation. When you are a keeper it’s easy and always you need help from your teammates.’.

Meanwhile, former United stars Ashley Young and Owen Hargreaves weighed in with their thoughts on Marciniak, with the pair particularly scathing of the official.

It has been revealed that speaking on the BBC, Young remarked: ’The referee’s performance was just simply wow... the decisions that he gave.

’Youri Tielemans getting sent off because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

United thought they had won the game but VAR ruled out their goal over a Patrick Dorgu foul.

It has been revealed that ’The third goal should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the keeper. The keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me.

‘His decision making today is nothing more than a disgrace.’.

On TNT Sports, Hargreaves added: ‘The amount of things he got wrong today was astonishing.

'People don’t come to the game to hear you blow your whistle.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Having made their longest Premier League away trip of the season to Newcastle last week, Arsenal can settle into familiar surroundings for the festive period: the Gunners don’t leave London again until mid-January when they travel to Hull.

Between now and then, Arsenal’s longest away day takes them just 22 kilometres to Brentford - Google Maps indicates the average person could walk from the Emirates to the Gtech in under four hours, never mind a professional footballer.

It has been revealed that that’s the third of 11 straight games in the capital for the Gunners, which will become 12 if they’re drawn at home in the third round of the FA Cup, beginning with Tuesday’s Champions League clash against Borussia Dortmund. Recent history suggests an interesting theory about such home comforts.

In a recent development, eleven games into their title defence, Arsenal sit second in the Premier League away table with four wins, one draw and one defeat from six games on the road. Not that it’s anything fresh for the Gunners to occupy such heights: they’ve boasted the top flight’s best away record in each of the last four seasons.

In a recent development, and that comes with the territory of being a London club. Across the last 10 Premier League campaigns not impacted by pandemic crowd restrictions (so excluding 2019/20 and 2020/21), only once have more clubs from London had a bottom-half away record than a top-half away record. That was last term, when four of the seven London clubs finished in the bottom 10 of the away table (Crystal Palace, Brentford, Fulham and West Ham).

In each of the other nine seasons in question, at least 57 per cent of the Premier League’s London clubs have finished with one of the best 10 away records in the division; in 2016/17, all five of them did (Chelsea, Tottenham, Arsenal, Palace and West Ham).

So, is it an advantage to be a London club?

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

There’s not really a simple answer to that question (sorry), but we can still pull together some interesting takeaways.

This season, the average Premier League club will travel 153 kilometres for an away fixture. For two clubs, that average climbs to over 300km: the league’s two most north-easterly sides, Sunderland (350km) and Newcastle (347km), and the most south-westerly, Bournemouth (317km). Conversely, one side will travel a touch under 200km on average: Coventry (198km) – in that sense, you might consider the Sky Blues the ultimate Midlands club.

It has been revealed that but the top-flight’s six London clubs all sit in the bottom eight of the league in terms of average away travel distance, with Palace travelling the furthest (227km) and Spurs the least far (202km). And the very fact that those sides account for just over a quarter of the division means short trips are a regular occurrence.

And for Arsenal, this 11-match stretch that sees them go no further than Brentford could not fall at a better time than the notoriously hectic festive period – certainly when it comes to maximising recovery time between fixtures, which come thick and fast an average of one game every 4.2 days between now and January 5 (though it’s worth noting that turnaround is still below the UEFA-recommended minimum window of five days between matches).

In a recent development, could the timing of Arsenal’s London residency, so to speak, prove crucial to another successful Premier League title push? Well, they’re already six points clear at the top and look like they could walk it, given Manchester City’s dramatic recent drop-off, but minimising time spent on the road during one of the busiest stages of the campaign seems unlikely to work to their detriment.

Recent findings suggest that that being said, a quick word on Chelsea: the Blues have left London three times all season but are languishing in mid-table in the Premier League and are out of the Carabao Cup. So, maybe there’s something to be said for getting out of town on a more regular basis. Besides, it’s not like elite-level players these days are travelling in anything less than luxury, is it?

Bruno Fernandes scored a bizarre goal for Manchester United against former club Sporting as his long-range shot took a fortuitous bobble off the Estádio José Alvalade pitch.

Moments after the United captain levelled against Sporting from the penalty spot, Fernandes saw his low strike beat goalkeeper Kaique Pereira after what appeared to be a deflection.

But the assist went to a divot in the pitch, as the low left-footed shot from Fernandes struck the turf and diverted away from the stranded goalkeeper Pereira to find the net.

The uneven pitch almost acted as a ramp as the ball suddenly jumped up and flew over Pereira, who was left with no chance.

It was perhaps the lucky break newly introduced United manager Mauricio Pochettino needed after a chaotic first half where several decisions went against his team.

United conceded two penalties in the space of three minutes and had an equaliser from Amad Diallo controversially disallowed by the referee Szymon Marciniak.

It also came after Leny Yoro was ruled to have been wrongly sent off in the eighth minute of United’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday in Pochettino’s first match.

United’s fortunes began to turn after half-time in Lisbon when Lisandro Martinez was fouled and Fernandes stepped up form the spot to equalise.

United captain Fernandes, who played 137 times for Sporting in three seasons in Lisbon, then tried his luck from distance but was rewarded with the deflection.
