Andreatta's masterplan to shock Sweden & take Scots to World Cup

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scotland women play Sweden in Paisley next Tuesday, with the second leg in Stockholm on 5 December.
  • Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", according to women's head coach Melissa Andreatta.
  • Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland women play Sweden in Paisley next Tuesday, with the second leg in Stockholm on 5 December.

Scotland intend to bring fancied Sweden's World Cup dream "crashing down - and do it in a truly Scottish way", according to women's head coach Melissa Andreatta.

Scotland face a two-legged World Cup qualifying play-off against powerhouses Sweden, who are managed by Andreatta's former boss Tony Gustavsson.

The Swedes, who have been semi-finalists at the two previous Women's World Cups and are ranked eighth in the world, will be strong favourites to reach the tournament in Brazil next summer.

Andreatta, who has eight wins, two losses and four draws from her 14 games in charge of Scotland, was Gustavsson's deputy when he was Australia head coach from 2020 to 2024.

While the two have a connection from those years, the Australian is very much in business mode with next week's first leg at St Mirren Park looming.

"A few weeks ago Tony reached out, sent me a few messages and I took my time to respond," she told BBC Scotland.

"It wasn't much about football, just connecting on a personal level - which is probably a good thing, because I can be quite competitive. I just want to focus on business and not the personal level.

"I'm sure, like he is, all we're focused on is how we're going to win.".

Listen to the full interview with Melissa Andreatta.

The Scots finished top of their qualifying group earlier this year after four wins from their six games before beating the Czech Republic 5-2 on aggregate in the play-off semi-final.

That set up the exacting play-off final against the Swedes, a team who narrowly missed out on a spot in the final at the previous two World Cups.

Scotland have made just one appearance at the tournament, in 2019, and Andreatta is excited by the prospect of getting one over her old boss for her latest home.

"It's going to be a great occasion to face them at home first," she added.

"They are such a powerhouse nation that carries so much expectation to go to their next tournament. We want to bring that all crashing down and do that in a truly Scottish way. That's what we're going to focus on.

"I definitely won't be looking at their dug out, I'll be focused on us and what we need to do to get the result and go to another tournament.

"They are an exceptional team but we won't be swayed by a team's reputation or ranking.

"We firmly believe that anything is possible. Once that whistle goes, if you've done the work and you're prepared you're in the position to make anything happen. With this group of players and staff I know that's possible, we can take it to anyone on any given day.

"It is a massive challenge but we love those moments and that's why we're here. We've earned it.".

Melissa Andreatta with daughter Mackenzie after Scotland beat the Czech Republic in their World Cup qualification semi-final.

There are more than 10,000 miles between Brisbane - where Andreatta grew up - and Ayr in Scotland, where she now calls home.

While the climate may be vastly different, there's one thing they do have in common - the beach.

"I love the coastal life. In Australia it's a big part of your lifestyle, being outdoors. I think there's something about the sea, being near it. Relaxing, calming, balancing," she noted.

It has been 18 months since Andreatta was announced as Pedro Martinez Losa's successor as manager of the Scotland women's team and now, with her family alongside her - including two-year-old daughter Mackenzie - she feels at home.

"We've definitely settled in," she added. "We have the spots that we go to, our routine, we love it here. It's been a great landing spot for us on such a massive move.".

But what does her daughter make of her mum's job?

It has been revealed that "She's got no idea," says Andreatta. "She just think's mum's on TV. Whenever she sees me she gets excited. Having her at the games is super special, being able to hold her on the pitch. She's such a joy.

"You do these things to make people proud and I want to make her proud.".

Andreatta has made a promising start as Scotland manager - but now faces a huge task.

Scotland without captain Weir for World Cup play-off.

New strategy released to transform Scottish women's football over 10 years.

Andreatta was sitting in the pubs of Scotland over the summer as the Tartan Army headed over to the United States in their droves to watch the men's team compete at a first World Cup in almost 30 years.

The women won't have to wait that long if they can book a spot on the plane to Brazil next summer.

Andreatta is hoping to see just as many kilts on the Copacabana beach as there were in the bars of Boston.

"There is a strong desire among the group, not only players but also the staff, there is this desire to make their nation proud and show Scotland that the women's national team belongs here and deserves as much of the limelight as the men's," she added.

Recent findings suggest that "Together we can make our nation proud and what better way to do it? To have our men at the World Cup and then the following summer our women.

It has been revealed that "Watching from afar, what the fans did over there and in Boston, why can't we do that in Rio? That's what I'm envisaging but there's a lot to do and achieve before we get there.".

COP31: No agreement on climate science, disinformation spreading

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (970 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The annual UN climate conference is the place where countries negotiate the world's aims to limit global warming and adapt to its consequences — and who will pay for climate action as well as damage from storms, floods and droughts.
  • But this year at COP31 in Antalya, an ongoing dispute over the timing of a key assessment of global warming is risking the scientific foundations of global climate action, say observers.
  • "We are extremely concerned about the situation," said a diplomat with the European delegation who could not speak on the record, adding that it came down to the future of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the world's leading body of climate scientists.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The annual UN climate conference is the place where countries negotiate the world's aims to limit global warming and adapt to its consequences — and who will pay for climate action as well as damage from storms, floods and droughts.

But this year at COP31 in Antalya, an ongoing dispute over the timing of a key assessment of global warming is risking the scientific foundations of global climate action, say observers.

"We are extremely concerned about the situation," said a diplomat with the European delegation who could not speak on the record, adding that it came down to the future of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the world's leading body of climate scientists.

Sources indicate that the IPCC's scientific assessments, published every six to seven years, provide the basis for major international climate agreements, including the 2015 Paris Agreement. The IPCC began evaluating the latest climate science in 1988 and its most recent report was published in 2023.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Researchers should have actually already started work on the next edition but the last plenary session was put on hold in October at the urging of Russia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and Kenya.

"The IPCC finds itself in a difficult situation," a spokesperson from the German Environment Ministry told DW at COP. "We stand ready to help resolve this issue, so that the panel can continue its work. To that end, we are holding many discussions with various countries to explore possible solutions.".

At the core of the dispute is the question of whether future UN climate talks base their negotiations on the latest scientific knowledge — or not.

That's especially relevant for the next "global stocktake," due in 2028, a report card on the world's climate efforts, which will shape action plans for countries around the world to lower planet-heating greenhouse gas emissions.

Recent findings suggest that the European Union, Brazil, the United Kingdom, small island states and several other countries especially at risk of the effects of climate change have called for the IPCC's seventh assessment report to be published in 2028, so it can be used to inform next steps for climate action. The report covers climate protection and impact.

"It's much more difficult without these scientific reports. Otherwise, we're just talking to ourselves or relying on information that's no longer current," stated a delegation source.

But Russia, Iran, India and Saudi Arabia want the IPCC report postponed until 2029, after the global stocktake.

The official reason: the tight timeline would be detrimental to the quality of the research, and could hinder the participation of researchers and governments representing developing countries.

Disagreements over budget issues have also held up the IPCC's work. Among other expenses, the funds are used to pay the travel arrangements for the hundreds of volunteer scientists, especially those from poorer countries, to attend the IPCC sessions.

"No budget means no more IPCC," said a member from another delegation, also speaking on condition of anonymity.

It hasn't come to that point yet, but without planning certainty the whole process risks being delayed — along with the climate negotiations that depend on this knowledge.

Researchers with the IPCC, however, have mentioned the timeline is attainable.

"We have no time to lose," said an open letter released in October signed by more than 100 researchers from 36 countries — including India and China. "We stand committed to continue working to deliver the [seventh assessment report] in a manner that is rigorous, timely and inclusive.".

But while the dispute over the timeline won't alter the scientific findings themselves, it could delay their political impact.

In its pre-COP communications, France accused the countries delaying the report's publication schedule of attempting to "obstruct science in order to lower the ambition of the global stocktake.".

The IPCC isn't a stranger to attempts at political persuasion: At past climate conferences, delegates from many countries have regularly negotiated the exact phrasing of the summary reports intended for policymakers.

Speaking at COP31 on November 17, EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra mentioned it was "fundamental to protect the integrity of climate science and the role of the IPCC as the source of best available science.".

Although there is no vote on the IPCC at COP31, it's possible that its significance and a timeline for the next report will be included in the final declaration of the climate talks, expected this weekend.

The IPCC has been warning for years that disinformation is hindering global climate action. And the struggle for information and control over the narrative in Antalya hasn't just been limited to the IPCC.

This was apparent in a document DW obtained that had been sent anonymously to several less wealthy countries' delegations in the run-up to COP31.

It claimed to explain the nature of Turkey's proposed goals for boosting electrification to 35% by 2035, but went on to misrepresent several core details of the plans to make them seem less appealing to developing countries than they are in reality.

At least two countries confirmed to DW that they had received the document. It did not state where it hailed from and was labeled as an "equity assessment.".

It has been revealed that the presentation portrays electrification as a business venture undertaken by wealthy countries at the expense of poorer nations. The International Energy Agency, however, has calculated that developing countries could save around $100 billion (€90 billion) in fossil fuel imports by 2035 through electrification.

Sources indicate that the presentation also gives the impression that all countries must meet fixed electrification targets. In fact, according to the UN, the 35% target represents a global goal, with individual countries free to determine their own national pathways.

This article was originally written in German.

Tottenham Hotspur are resurgent in the Premier League – but that hasn't stopped one player's agent from linking his client with a move out of N17.

FourFourTwo understands that Spurs don't expect to do very much business in the winter window, with the likes of Jan Paul van Hecke, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush signed over the summer in a £400 million spree that saw Tottenham smash their transfer record twice.

But while the summer saw significant departures, there could well be more where that came from this January, with one star publicly angling to leave.

The Lilywhites have won four of their last five fixtures in the league and turned their form around, as they look to bounce back from back-to-back 17th-placed finishes.

With plenty of interest in Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney from the likes of Manchester United and Newcastle, however, Spurs could see an opportunity to move on a wantaway fringe player from their squad.

Sport Witness have relayed an interview from Al-Maidan with Richarlison’s agent, Fidel Carvalho Soares, in which the Brazilian has been mentioned as a target for the Saudi Pro League.

Richarlison came close to an exit over the summer from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium but after the transfer fell through, he hasn't played under manager Roberto De Zerbi this term, with his future at the club to be decided in January.

“What is being said about negotiations between Al-Ahli and the player are just rumours,” Soares said, “However, Richarlison would welcome the opportunity to play in the Saudi league soon.

The agent added that Trabzonspor made an official offer over the summer but after the North Londoners rejected the bid, the Turkish side haven't been in contact again to rekindle the embers of a move.

Man United turn Champions League into Sunday League to highlight glaring problem

  • Two errors from Senne Lammens denied Mauricio Pochettino his first win as Manchester United manager as his side slipped to a 2-2 draw with Sporting in a bizarre match in Lisbon.
  • It has been revealed that those watching were treated to three penalties, a late red card and a ridiculous goal – courtesy of a divot in the pitch – as the sides played out a entertaining affair in the Portuguese capital.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Two errors from Senne Lammens denied Mauricio Pochettino his first win as Manchester United manager as his side slipped to a 2-2 draw with Sporting in a bizarre match in Lisbon.

It has been revealed that those watching were treated to three penalties, a late red card and a ridiculous goal – courtesy of a divot in the pitch – as the sides played out a entertaining affair in the Portuguese capital. However, once again the focus will all be on United and their comedy of errors, as the visitors let a 2-1 lead slip late on in remarkable fashion.

United have had several pantomime villains of late and it was the turn of the goalkeeper this time, with Lammens conceding a penalty and inexplicably dropping a simple catch to give the hosts an 80th-minute equaliser.

Pochettino insisted that his players “are not fragile” in the build-up to the match but he was proven wrong in spectacular fashion here.

A momentary lapse in concentration from Lammens near his own goal line turned out to be a foreshadowing, though United had settled well in Lisbon, with the visitors enjoying a long period of control midway into the first half.

They lacked a cutting edge in their attacking but they at least looked comfortable, which is not something that has been remarked at all in recent matches. And yet once again it all changed in a matter of minutes.

Lisandro Martinez, this time filling in at left-back, was once again the culprit, with the defender needlessly swinging a leg at Geny Catamo and inviting the winger to go down in the box. It was soft but it should not take away from the fact that it’s yet another high-profile mistake from the Argentine.

The momentum of the game changed instantly, though United threatened to stop it when Lammens guessed the right way to stop Luis Suarez’s poor spot-kick.

But there was still time for more of the ridiculous – as has been a theme at the club this season – and just minutes after saving a penalty, Lammens had conceded one.

According to recent reports, the goalkeeper ventured off his line but failed to win the challenge on Maxi Araujo, who left Noussair Mazraoui in no man’s land to latch onto the long ball and poke it past the helpless Belgian. This time, Suarez made no mistake.

Sporting fans were clearly aware of United’s frailties and the Jose Alvalade was a cauldron of noise as the hosts looked to build on their lead, though the visitors managed to stem the tide as they grew back into the game.

Amad thought he had equalised before half-time, only for referee Szymon Marciniak to blow up for a soft foul by Youri Tielemans, who looked to have won the ball in the build-up with a sliding challenge on Goncalo Inacio on the edge of the box. It was another decision that will raise questions and once again United seemed down on their luck as the two sides went in for half-time.

It has been revealed that but just as their fortunes had changed in a flash in the first half, the visitors found themselves back in the game through their own slice of luck, with Martinez robbing Eduardo Quaresma near his own box before driving into the area and going down under a challenge from the Portuguese. It was soft, but Pochettino might have felt it deserved. Up stepped Bruno Fernandes against his old club, with the Portuguese powering his effort low and into the corner to level the game in the 48th minute.

And if the penalty was a slice of luck then United were soon served the entire cake, with the visitors finding themselves 2-1 up just two minutes after going level. Fernandes took a speculative effort from range, but it paid off as it skipped through the bodies and hit a divot in the box before flying over a helpless Kaique in goal.

Industry observers note that the Champions League had briefly turned into Sunday League but United did not care. In fact, looking at the intensity and fervour in their celebrations, you could tell it was desperately needed.

And the visitors were on top after going ahead, but the sense that there is plenty of danger whenever any ball comes towards their box remains, and for good reason.

A poor cross from the right provoked groans among the home fans but it was enough to test Lammens, with the Belgian flapping at it and spilling it straight to Suarez, who produced an accomplished overhead finish to level the scores in the 80th minute.

It was a perfect error to sum up a truly bizarre 90 minutes in Lisbon, and while there was time for more of the ridiculous – with Tielemans picking up a second yellow card and United having a third ruled out for a foul on the goalkeeper from Dorgu – it was not a game that United deserved to win.

In a recent development, that might not be what worries Pochettino most. Rather, the new United boss will privately be concerned with the errors that his players keep making, from Yoro’s red card last week to Lammens’ horror show tonight.

One error is exactly that, but consistent errors at vital times when the pressure is on points to something else entirely. It is a double-edged sword, with an obvious mentality issue but the additional problem that the team keeps putting itself in territory where mistakes can be made, either from poor defending, simple mistakes or just from a lack of control.

Indeed, the Argentine highlighted “things we need to improve, details we need to work [on]” during his post-match conference, while pointing to a need to be strong in terms of “mentality”.

One could argue that United would be in a good position if they could iron out these errors, but that argument is a useless one when they keep happening.

These errors were a problem before Pochettino, but they are now his glitch to deal with. United do have frailties, and he might find that removing them and restoring some confidence is the first step in rehabilitating his struggling side.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Beattie won the last of her 13 caps last year while the uncapped Haughey was last called into the senior squad in 2021.

Michael McArdle has decided the upcoming friendly double-header against Greece is the perfect time to bring back Kerry Beattie and Ella Haughey from the international wilderness.

Glentoran midfielder Chloe McCarron is also in under McArdle for the first time after a lengthily absence, but the Glentoran midfielder would likely have been included sooner if not for a spell on the sidelines through injury.

Beattie won her last cap a year ago while Haughey will hope to make a senior debut in one of the two games against Greece at Inver Park after she was an unused substitute in friendlies against England and Scotland in her sole call up in 2021.

The inclusion of both players, who have been in good form at their clubs, shows McArdle is willing to keep the door open for a return to the international squad if players are performing at club level.

Magill returns to NI squad for Greece friendlies.

Beattie has four goals in her 13 NI caps.

Portsmouth striker Beattie has been in and out of squads since her debut in 2021.

The 24-year-old has four goals in 13 caps, the last of which she won against Iceland in the Nations League play-off a year ago.

A prolific forward during two spells at Glentoran, she has struggled for consistency in moves across to Scotland with the likes of Glasgow City, Hearts and Aberdeen.

She left the Dons in the summer and consulted with McArdle when deciding upon her next move, before joining WSL 2 side Portsmouth.

Beattie has eight goals in all competitions for a Pompey side languishing at the bottom of the table and McArdle is pleased she has settled in well.

"Kerry had spells at Hearts and Aberdeen and for whatever reason it didn't quite work out at both, she had good spells but not a consistent run to express herself," McArdle said.

It has been revealed that "The move to Portsmouth, I was delighted she reached out to me for some advice, it's an alignment for her and it's been a great move on and off the pitch. It's allowed her to enjoy herself but also play 90 minutes and be that focal point striker.

"She will have been disappointed not to make the squad for the [World Cup] play-off [against Portugal] with her form but she worked hard and she's back in, I'm delighted for her.".

Beattie faces stiff competition for the starting striker role from the likes of returning captain Simone Magill and Kess Elmore, who impressed in the last camp and scored against Portugal, but she should receive some minutes across the two games and will be keen to grasp her chance to make an impact.

Left-back Haughey was called up to the senior squad as a 16-year-old under Kenny Shiels, but did not feature.

West Brom defender Haughey's last involvement with NI came when she represented the under-19s in 2023.

A Lisburn Rangers player when Kenny Shiels included her in the senior squad as a 16-year-old, Haughey then moved to Nottingham Forest before settling at the Baggies, who play in the National League.

The left-back, 22, has been a regular this season for the club in the third tier and combines playing with her university studies.

Left-back has been a problem position for NI which McArdle has been trying to address as demonstrated by him bringing in Lucy-Jayne Grant in the last camp and Haughey for this window to allow Rebecca Holloway to play as a central defender.

Haughey will be competing with Grant to fill that full-back role on the left side and McArdle believes she is more than capable of doing so having tried to bring her back into the squad earlier in his reign.

Sources indicate that "Ella's been at West Brom for a few years now. She has real potential, strong, athletic potential. We tried to call her up sooner but there were some challenges," he explained.

It has been revealed that "She's probably been one of their top performers and one of the top performers in the league. Delighted she's earned this opportunity and hopefully she can make her debut and achieve her first cap.".

McArdle has made a concerted to continue to widen the player pool available to him as he aims to build depth ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, but if Beattie and Haughey catch the eye it will show that giving chances to those previously involved under different managers could be another possibility.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aerial scenery of Hengqin Free Trade Zone, China. Credit: Weiming Xie/Shutterstock.

Sources indicate that two-thirds of the world’s population will be living in cities by 2050, according to the latest estimates by the United Nations. Coinciding with the mass movement of people into urban areas is the rapid integration of technology into many of those spaces. From automated subterranean waste-collection systems to driverless vehicle zones, these ‘smart-city’ solutions are changing the way that people live, work and move through their environments.

Some cities are embracing these technological advances at a much faster pace than others. Places such as Beijing, Helsinki, London and Singapore stand out for the way they are integrating smart-city technology into existing infrastructure and services.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Nature Index 2026 Science cities.

Other cities are emerging with these technologies integral to their operations from their inception. But as the examples of Songdo in South Korea and Hengqin in China illustrate, building smart infrastructure from scratch is only half the challenge: these places must also attract and retain the research and innovation talent needed to develop, operate and improve it. It’s a ‘chicken-and-egg’ problem, says Songdo-based urban-planning researcher, Dakota McCarty: talent follows world-class universities and thriving economic zones, which need a critical mass of expertise and investment to be attractive.

Breaking: England, Northern Ireland, Scotland & Wales to host 2035 Women's World Cup

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.
  • It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.
  • The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain beat England 1-0 to win the 2023 World Cup.

England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales will jointly host the 2035 Women's World Cup, Fifa has confirmed.

It will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the United Kingdom since the men's tournament in 1966.

The four countries were the only bidders for the tournament, and were ratified as co-hosts at a specially arranged virtual meeting from Fifa's Zurich headquarters.

The tournament will consist of 104 matches contested by 48 teams over 39 days.

The 'All Together' bid included a proposal to use 19 venues, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

Monday's special meeting of Fifa's Congress also approved the joint bid by Mexico, the United States, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031 finals, which will be the first to feature 48 teams.

The news comes on the same day the UK government announced a vision for one million more girls to play, watch or be in leadership roles in sport by the time the tournament takes place.

Hosting World Cup means decade of excitement - Weir.

Fifa announces UK will host 2035 Women's World Cup.

England failed to win the right to host the men's World Cups in 2006 and 2018, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for the 2030 tournament was abandoned.

But England and Scotland hosted matches at the men's Euros in 2021, and England staged the women's European Championship in 2022, which the Lionesses won.

England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland will jointly host the men's European Championship in 2028.

Mark Bullingham, chief executive of the Football Association, said: "Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play.

"Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.".

The English stadiums included in the 2035 bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, the Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

If Manchester United's proposed latest Old Trafford stadium does not go ahead, it would still be considered in its current form.

Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium are the two Welsh venues, with Easter Road in Edinburgh and Hampden Park in Glasgow in Scotland.

Northern Ireland missed out on co-hosting the men's Euros in 2028 after the UK government stated in 2024 it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time - but a redeveloped Windsor Park is set to stage matches in 2035.

A further three stadiums could be added - Birmingham's new Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham's redeveloped Racecourse Ground, and a potential new Chelsea ground - which would take the tournament to 16 cities and 22 venues.

Fifa is yet to decide whether all four co-hosts will qualify automatically.

The Principality Stadium in Cardiff is one of two Welsh venues, along with the Cardiff City Stadium.

The participation of women and girls in football has risen by 2.3m since the Women's European Championship was held in England in 2022.

However, women remain significantly underrepresented in leadership positions.

Only a quarter of chief executive, chair or performance director roles in major UK sports are held by women and only 12% of sports federations are led by a female.

Noel Mooney, the chief executive of the Football Association of Wales, noted: "This is a proud day for Welsh football.

"We've put forward Wrexham and Cardiff as host cities, and it's exciting to think what a World Cup could bring to both cities and the communities around them.

Sources indicate that "In Llunio Cymru - our 10-year strategy - we've set ourselves the ambition of reaching the knockout stages in 2035. Some of the players who could take us there are learning the game at clubs across Wales today. Our job is to make sure that wherever a girl grows up in Wales, she can find a team close to home, have a coach who helps her develop and see a route to the Cymru shirt.".

Irish Football Association chief executive Patrick Nelson said the event "would be felt in every club and every age group, in every part of the country".

"Our young players would grow up having watched the best in the world play at home, and there is no substitute for that," he added.

Scottish Football Association chief executive Ian Maxwell noted hosting the tournament would be "the most significant thing to happen to the women's and girls' game in Scotland".

Sources indicate that he added: "The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.".

Fifa's evaluation, published earlier this month, rated the bid 4.3 out of five. Its contractual framework was rated 'medium risk', and the document claimed "certain government guarantees contain material qualifications, particularly regarding tax and safety and security".

That is thought to refer to a lack of agreement over a request by Fifa for tax-free status for all football-related activities.

The bid evaluation noted: "The bidder has submitted an extensive set of government support documents and contractual hosting agreements, demonstrating the commitment of the relevant authorities and stakeholders.

"However, certain government guarantees, particularly those relating to safety and security and tax, contain certain qualifications which have been duly noted in the legal evaluation.

"While certain contractual matters remain subject to further discussion, the bidder's proactive engagement with Fifa and the substantial lead-in time provide a sound basis for resolving these outstanding challenges.".

Industry observers note that for Manchester City, life after three Champions League-winning midfielders began in earnest against Arsenal in August. They were a goal down after 23 seconds. It was an inauspicious start for Enzo Maresca and Elliot Anderson alike.

In a recent development, A reunion with Arsenal on Sunday could be deemed a meeting of managerial midfielders, in Maresca and Mikel Arteta. Each learned from Pep Guardiola, who won the European Cup as a Barcelona player and manager and then in charge of City. But it is also a first Premier League clash since Bernardo Silva and Rodri joined their mentor in decamping from the Etihad Stadium in the summer. Arsenal may not have been sorry to see any go; if Guardiola’s resignation could facilitate an era of dominance from Arteta, and if it may have already begun with last season’s Premier League title, a further factor could be the departures of the City captain and Spain’s World Cup-winning skipper.

In a recent development, if City have been confronted with the question of how to replace the irreplaceable, there are different answers. One is simply that it is impossible: they are irreplaceable. Another is: expensively. City committed £326m to three midfield recruits, in Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez. A third is: incoherently, at least so far. Perhaps it is unfair to expect newcomers, both in the dugout and the centre of the pitch, to bring the same cohesion and chemistry as predecessors who became the faces of longevity and continuity, but thus far they have not.

Industry observers note that A further subplot, arguably, is that Arsenal boast men who represented an alternative line of succession at City: not merely Arteta, Guardiola’s first assistant in Manchester, but Bruno Guimaraes, who was of interest at the Etihad in 2024, but when City chose not to activate his release clause, and Declan Rice, the target who preferred to join Arsenal in 2023. Arguably the England vice-captain was the best central midfielder in the Premier League even with Rodri and Silva; without them, and despite Pascal Gross’ extraordinary start to the season, he definitely is.

According to recent reports, but if Arsenal won the war last season, City prevailed in the battles, based around the formidable double act of Silva and Rodri. They faced the Gunners three times; but for Gabriel Martinelli’s injury-time equaliser at the Emirates Stadium, they would have won all three. Rodri’s prowess then may have come at a cost: it was his third start in a week, and he only began two more games in the next three months. City had barely a third of the ball, in an anti-Pep performance, but were superb out of possession.

Recent findings suggest that in March’s Carabao Cup final, Nico O’Reilly’s box-crashing brace earned him the man-of-the-match award, but victory was underpinned by the midfield platform constructed by the Portuguese and the Spaniard. Finally, in City’s Premier League win at the Etihad, when victory seemed to shift the initiative to them in the title race, Silva was talismanic and terrific, turning in one of the best of his 460 performances for City. Two astonishing defensive interventions, one running back with Kai Havertz, the other winning a header against the rather taller Viktor Gyokeres, led Erling Haaland to compare him to Fabio Cannavaro.

Sources indicate that that influence, that drive, that capacity to perform in major matches: perhaps it was inevitably irreplaceable, just as Rodri’s Golden Ball-winning World Cup showed no other defensive midfielder can be as good as him. The first three-and-a-half months of Maresca’s reign have shown City lack anyone who is knitting the team together as well as Rodri and Silva did. A susceptibility to the counter-attack could be a flaw in the Guardiola years, but has been more so without the two men charged with cutting them out.

It has been compounded by some of the stranger structural issues. Fernandez has spent some of his time in the inside-right channel, some apparently with designs of being a No 10. Anderson has often been isolated. He has been excellent, but even a £116m midfielder can only cover so much ground on his own.

Maresca has tended to use the word “balance”, reflecting City’s quest for it. The most obvious answer involves introducing Bouaddi alongside Anderson: the times Fernandez has played with most positional discipline have at least involved some of the bigger games, whether away at Porto, in a Manchester derby when down to 10 men or at Anfield. But City’s openness in midfield was exploited by Paris Saint-Germain: Bouaddi, a half-time remedy, brought improvement.

There is a sense that City may have complicated the equation with the Enzo reunion, Maresca’s £125m move for his former Chelsea ally Fernandez. The Argentinian’s fondness for operating in the final third can impact upon Rayan Cherki and Phil Foden; instead of a third possible No 10, City could have done more with another player with the skillset of Guimaraes or his old Newcastle sidekick Sandro Tonali, players who can be a No 6 or a No 8, in the mould of Anderson.

It has been revealed that but maybe the task for Fernandez, Anderson, Bouaddi and Maresca always threatened to be thankless. Coming after Rodri and Silva in midfield or Guardiola in the technical area ran the risk anyone would be an automatic downgrade. And maybe Arsenal will underline that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City are considering the future of manager Enzo Maresca, just 19 games into the Italian's stint.

After Pep Guardiola led the Citizens to 20 trophies in a decade-long tenure, Manchester City turned to Maresca to take charge of the club, with the former Leicester City and Chelsea boss having worked at the Etihad as both the under-23s manager and as one of Guardiola's assistants in the 2022/23 Treble-winning campaign.

But with uncertainty shrouding the club – following an independent commission finding City guilty of over 100 breaches of serious financial rules across a nine-year period – things may be about to become even more unstable, should the six-time Premier League champions pull the trigger on their manager already.

Maresca started fantastically after taking over from his former mentor, winning his first seven Premier League games – including a defiant 3-0 thumping of Liverpool at Anfield following the news that City had been found guilty and were facing Premier League sanctions.

But the Eastlands outfit went on to lose the following three games in the league, drew against Fulham at the weekend, and had to rely on a late Rayan Cherki equaliser against Napoli last night in order to scrape a point in the Champions League.

Fichajes in Spain are reporting that Maresca “will be fighting for his job” if he doesn't beat Arsenal this weekend, with the Gunners having already outclassed his side 3-0 in the Community Shield earlier this season.

A defeat at the Emirates Stadium would widen the gap between the pair to a seemingly unassailable nine points, with Liverpool and surprise package Brighton & Hove Albion shaping up to be the champions' biggest threats in completing back-to-back league championships for the first time in almost a century.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

While City started the season emphatically, fans have questioned several tactical decisions – and after netting seven in his first seven fixtures, talismanic centre-forward Erling Haaland has cut a frustrated figure while leading the line.

Record signing Enzo Fernandez has blown hot and cold this season and kept the mercurial Cherki out of the side at times, Marc Guehi has started the season slowly with shaky performances from centre-back, and Phil Foden has been in disappointing form in the league, though he netted a hat-trick against AEK Athens in the Champions League.

Several of Guardiola's generals have been linked with exits, with Haaland's future in doubt, while Barcelona have interest in Josko Gvardiol to fill a problem position at left-back.

Despite the autumnal wobble, however, FourFourTwo understands that there are no prepares at present to part with Maresca.

The Italian was handed a three-year deal over the summer to succeed Guardiola, with BBC Sport reporting that City paid around £17 million to Maresca's former club Chelsea as a compensation fee after he left the Blues in January 2026, following run of just one win in seven league games.

City's clash with Arsenal is set for 4.30pm this Sunday as Premier League action resumes.

Joshua Kimmich has hammered his own club Bayern Munich for their 'incomprehensible' and 'unacceptable' undermining of Jamal Musiala's ongoing illness battle.

Musiala, the 23-year-old golden boy of German football, has hardly played this season due to seizures brought on by 'neurological dysfunction' and has an £18m-a-year salary until 2030.

Last week, Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the club could discuss him taking a pay cut, arguing: 'We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible.

‘I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.'.

There was a huge outcry after Rummenigge's remarks, with the likes of Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand all backing Musiala.

And when asked about the situation after Bayern's 2-1 defeat by Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Kimmich said: 'What happened now is something that simply must never happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.

Joshua Kimmich hammered Bayern Munich for their handling of Jamal Musiala's situation.

Musiala came off the bench for Bayern in their 2-1 defeat by Lille on Wednesday night.

'I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal's agent or with Jamal himself. And I think the other side is open to that as well.

It has been revealed that 'I believe I've also read that they've met and are supposed to problem a statement. What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It must never happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it.

Industry observers note that 'Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than us as players, but it's not bigger than the person. And that's an absolute no-go. It's also not the Bayern way. Especially at this particular time, when I've often emphasised how special this club is.

Sources indicate that 'Even in my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out.'.

Kimmich pointed out that Musiala's health issues are in no way a result of him being unprofessional.

'We mustn't forget that he underwent another operation in the summer and then suffered another injury afterwards,' he continued.

'But I see him and spend time with him every day. I see how he works and how hard he works. That's another key aspect of the situation. It's not as though he's having problems because he's unprofessional. Quite the opposite: he's here every day, naturally wants to get the very best out of himself, works extremely hard every day and, I think, genuinely enjoys being part of our team.

'I hope he knows that all of us are 100% behind him, both the team and the club officials.'.

While Kimmich offered his support to Musiala, he admitted he did understand the difficulty the club faces financially with one of their most expensive players unable to start more than one Bundesliga game this season.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

Sources indicate that he continued: 'Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I have absolute understanding for the fact that this is not an easy situation for a club either.

It has been revealed that 'Of course, I've witnessed Jamal's journey over the past two years. I mean, he carried us at the Euros and was our standout player afterwards. Then he signed a contract extension, was given the number 10 shirt here and with the German national team. Then came the first muscle injury. I can speak from personal experience: when you extend your contract, especially at that age, it's not about sitting back and enjoying the next five years.

'Rather, it's a source of motivation and a responsibility you want to live up to. Then Jamal had the illness and the serious injury. We mustn't forget that over the past year and a half, I don't think he's managed to play four or five games in a row.

Sources indicate that 'So it's understandable to some extent that he's not performing at his usual level. And it's also understandable that the club might be concerned because of the illness.'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen stated in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

In a recent development, 'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

In a recent development, 'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

In a recent development, 'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

'Money has become more vital than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Musiala came off the bench on Wednesday night against Lille and managed to play the final 15 minutes of the 2-1 defeat.

Tech Report: Palace docked points for using four sub windows in WSL win

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025.
  • Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.
  • Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025.

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.

Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.

However, manager Jo Potter brought on Kirsty Howat for Shannon O'Brien in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to try and shore up the victory.

It was the fourth separate substitution made by Potter, who had also made changes in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time wasting.

Crystal Palace deducted points following WSL win.

Palace have been stripped of the three points they earned in the match - one of only two WSL games the Eagles have won this season.

This punishment drops Palace down one place in the WSL table to 13th - the relegation play-off place.

Palace are now below fellow promoted side Birmingham City in the table on goal difference, with both sides now having six points - six behind Everton in 11th.

In a statement on their club website, external Palace stated they were "disappointed" by the decision.

The decision was made by an independent tribunal after Palace admitted the breach of competition rule 5.19.1.

The rule states: "A substitution can only be made when play is stopped for any reason and the referee has given permission. A club at its discretion may use five substitute players during a match. For the avoidance of doubt, each club has no more than three substitution opportunities in each match.".

The tribunal said that while the rule breach was inadvertent and "not intended to secure an unfair advantage", it said a points deduction was necessary in order to provide a deterrent to clubs against making a similar mistake in future.

"The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained, save in exceptional circumstances," the tribunal stated in its full written decision., external.

They said the lateness of the substitution in the match - so late that Howat did not touch the ball after coming on - did not excuse Palace from punishment.

It also ruled "that responsibility for complying with the rule rests with clubs, not match officials".

Palace - who placed the word "fourth" in inverted commas in their response to the ruling - are aiming to improve on their only previous WSL campaign in 2024-25, where they only won twice in 22 matches and were relegated by a 10-point margin.

Their statement read: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty â a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL.".

Forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith had scored the only goal of the game in the 34th minute on her Palace debut.

Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

In a recent development, it was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-footed thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyökeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

In a recent development, so it proved after 75 minutes when Gyökeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside a post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

It ended that way, with a heroic defensive performance from the Dortmund defence, including one memorable moment when substitute Serhou Guirassy’s determination to block a cross prompted a double ricochet off his own post. One could make the argument that there were times when it was “unbelievable”, as Arteta later mentioned, that the ball did not find its way in. Although there were also moments when the reasons were self-evident.

“There’s an element of luck,” the Arsenal manager mentioned, “and there is an element of us [not] finishing better.”.

In fifth place in the league phase table, dropped points at home do not carry the same jeopardy in the group stage that they once did, yet even so there was a truth for Arteta to chew upon. This is a well-honed, major-game Arsenal Champions League side that he has built. One that reached the final last season and may well go close again, but as ever they seem to be doing so in spite of the great goalscorer that so many of their nearest rivals have at their disposal.

Arteta sounded that warning after defeat in the final in Budapest at the end of May and, while changes have been made, it would be hard to argue that they have been fundamental. This was a good opponent – the leaders of the Bundesliga with many exports from English football who have been reconditioned for the German game. Those include Fábio Silva, Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham, who had a second-half goal narrowly disallowed for offside.

By Yannick HuberOn Tuesday, all eyes will be on Ethan Nwaneri. The Champions League clash between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund marks the 19-year-old’s return to the club where he grew up, where he became the Premier League’s youngest player and from whom he joined Dortmund on loan in the summer. It would be hard to imagine a more poignant setting. But for Nwaneri, facing Arsenal is about more than a reunion. It is also an opportunity to finally make his mark at Dortmund.

Sources indicate that so far his time in Germany has not gone according to strategy. Nwaneri arrived with a considerable reputation and high expectations, but has become less prominent in recent weeks. His playing time has diminished and he has frequently had to settle for a place on the bench.

But there are several reasons to believe that, of all games, this meeting with his former club could give his Dortmund career fresh impetus.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie; Rice, Lewis-Skelly; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; GyokeresSubs: Meslier, Porter, Saliba, Mosquera, Eze, Timber, Merino, Havertz, Calafiori, Guimaraes, Dowman.

Dortmund: Kobel, Ryerson, Anton, Schlotterbeck, Gadou, Svensson, Veerman, Nmecha, Bellingham, Beier, SilvaSubs: Drewes, Meyer, Bensebaini, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Nwaneri, Karetsas, Sabitzer, Mane, Albert, Dos Santos, Reggiani.

Mikel Arteta was an Arsenal player the last time they played Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, and tonight he will have to make do without first-choice goalkeeper David Raya.

Arsenal’s manager struck an upbeat note when describing the shoulder or upper arm injury Raya sustained at Newcastle, and it appears he has avoided a long-term absence.

Even two weeks out, however, would mean Raya missing Premier League fixtures against Manchester City, Brentford and Spurs – possibly Arsenal’s most testing week of the season. Arteta did not rule out a return to face City on Sunday.

Industry observers note that kepa Arrizabalaga is expected to deputise against Dortmund, who are top of the Bundesliga and have won three of their four Champions League league phase games. They won at the Emirates in a pre-season friendly, and Jobe Bellingham and on-loan Arsenal attacker Ethan Nwaneri are among their ranks.

These Champions League fixtures can feel secondary in importance to Premier League fare because of the competition’s fresh format, but a top-two finish in the league phase is a serious incentive.

As Arsenal discovered to their benefit last season when they “won” the league phase, the top two teams are rewarded with home second legs all the way to the final.

Arsenal are currently third on 10 points and face Real Madrid at the Emirates next, the team above them in second, so victory this evening is essential to set up that occasion.

Arteta has tended to make between four and six changes for these games, and Ben White, Piero Hincapie, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres are players pushing for starts after starting on the bench at Newcastle.

Also among the substitutes at St James’ Park was William Saliba, who is stepping up his return from a long-term back injury and could play his first minutes of the season tonight.

How Mauricio Pochettino can solve Man United’s bad luck problem

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (854 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later?
  • Mauricio Pochettino could only resort to basic logic.
  • For a match characterised by so much error, and often absurdity, United were actually encouragingly competent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Mauricio Pochettino could only resort to basic logic. “It’s difficult to understand,” the fresh Manchester United manager mentioned of various moments in his team’s chaotic 2-2 draw at Sporting CP. You could even extend that description to the logic of the performance.

For a match characterised by so much error, and often absurdity, United were actually encouragingly competent.

The basic organisation was better. The application was more intense. They probably should have won the game. And yet the reason they didn’t points to one of Pochettino’s bigger challenges, to go alongside imposing a tactical idea on this team.

According to recent reports, because, from one perspective, United were simply undone by blind bad luck. That statement arguably applies to each of Pochettino’s first two games, which is why it’s hard not to have at least some sympathy for the latest coach.

Against Liverpool, an entire first gameplan was undone by a controversial early red card for Leny Yoro that the FA have said should not have stood – amid considerable controversy. Against Sporting in the Champions League, among other decisions, a possible late winner was overruled by what felt a spurious decision.

With both, there was a sense of the odds being unfairly stacked at crucial moments. Pochettino had few other options against Liverpool and few remaining minutes against Sporting.

The very outlook from his first two games could have been entirely transformed. And it is that outlook which is especially crucial right now, given how low on confidence the team has been.

Their mood could have been transformed, too, and at a fragile moment.

Pochettino can do nothing about luck, after all; about the basic bounces of the ball – quite an irony given Bruno Fernandes’ second goal.

Sources indicate that that’s despite this being a club that arguably perpetuated the idea you make your own luck more than any in modern football. It was the entire lesson of the Ferguson era, especially the mythic treble season of 1998-99.

That United side, more than maybe any other European champions, just imposed their will on game after game. They never accepted setbacks or losing positions. They kept going until they manifested victory, regardless of anything else.

Recent findings suggest that the idea that this represented ‘making their own luck; was of course a myth, though. There were many moments when they got extremely fortunate, in a manner they could do nothing about.

That applies to everything from Dennis Bergkamp hitting a weak penalty in that FA Cup semi-final replay to Mehmet Scholl’s chip dropping onto the post rather than the inside netting in the Champions League final.

Many in football, and especially in their analytics departments, would caution that the effect of luck in football remains extremely under-appreciated.

It may even be the next most notable factor on the game after wages and recruitment.

Sources indicate that united’s whole 2026 could be cast as a case study. In Michael Carrick’s first five months, so many borderline moments went his way. In his last five, so many went against him.

The real concern was the effect, and the momentum.

In a recent development, because, if Pochettino or any other manager obviously have no control over their luck, they can control how they respond to it. This was probably the real lesson of the Ferguson era. It wasn’t making your own luck, it was making your own path in response.

United suffered multiple setbacks but just didn’t let it affect them. There was a Govan ironworks resilience, that has been entirely absent in this team.

Sources indicate that that’s how so many games have become so bad, when the 2026 version of United have simply looked beaten. It could be seen in this Sporting game.

Although United did start well, their belief dropped after the double penalty and they buckled.

As one insider said after the game, “there have just been so many ‘head’s gone’ defensive moments this season”.

Recent findings suggest that it speaks to that fragility. And that, as much as the tactics, is what Pochettino has to address. He needs to restore belief. It’s just as well this is known as one of his best qualities, regardless of the questions about how advanced his tactics are in the modern game.

There were signs he has made a start, which is why the way these opening two games went seems such a specific setback. Work was undone in the most unlucky ways that also had the most disproportionate effect.

The irony is that part of building resilience is to now dwell on that, to try and build a tunnel vision.

Pochettino is stated to feel he can do that with the majority of this squad, despite the doubts about personnel.

And that’s what this is all about: dispelling doubts. His United might not be able to make their own luck. But they can forge a new resilience.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool and Bayern Munich might be about to shake hands on an intriguing transfer move in which big names move on either side.

The last two summers have been two of the biggest transfer windows in Liverpool's history, with three £100 million players joining the club in a recruitment revolution, following the end of the Jurgen Klopp era.

And things might be about to get even more extraordinary, with Bayern Munich “increasingly likely” to sell one of their biggest names – and the Reds front and centre for his signature.

Despite critics pointing to a lack of balance in their forward options over the summer, Liverpool are starting to find rhythm in attack under upcoming manager Andoni Iraola, as the likes of Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Rio Ngumoha all performed well in the weekend's 4-1 victory over Manchester United.

With Wirtz and Ngumoha both targets of Bayern Munich, however, the balance may be about to shift again – with the Bavarians now “increasingly likely” to sell Jamal Musiala.

Musiala has struggled this season with what he has described as “neurological dysfunction” this season, with honourary Bayern president Uli Hoeness has faced significant criticism for comments in which he questioned whether Musiala will ever return to his best form for Die Roten, stating, “What he is capable of delivering now is no longer what was stipulated in the contract” he signed at the Allianz Arena.

TEAMtalk reports that Liverpool and Arsenal are now interested in Musiala, with Bayern now potentially open to selling a previously untouchable asset – paving the way for either Wirtz or Ngumoha to leave.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

FourFourTwo understands that the latter is in talks over a new contract, but with Wirtz having struggled in English football since briefly becoming the Reds' all-time record transfer, he may welcome a return to the Bundesliga, where he made a name for himself as one of the biggest talents in world football and won the title with an invincible Bayer Leverkusen side.

It has recently been suggested in the German media that Wirtz and Musiala aren't naturally compatible in the same team, with journalist Christian Falk likening the pair's jostling for a place as Die Mannschaft's No.10 as similar to the battle between Gunter Netzer and Wolfgang Overath for a place in West Germany's 1974 World Cup side.

Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard, meanwhile, has been linked with a move to Bayern – while the Gunners could field Musiala on the left wing.

In a recent development, transfermarkt values Musiala at €80m. Liverpool face Club Brugge tonight in Champions League action.

Boris Rosenfeld demonstrates DW a photo of him with his daughter Sofia and can't hold back tears. "This was the last time we saw her. Then she left for Moscow, and this whole case began," he says.

According to recent reports, helives in Israel, while Sofia is in Russia. For more than a month now, she has been behind bars on charges of financing extremism. On October 7, a court in Moscow sentenced Rosenfeld to three and a half years in a penal colony.

Rosenfeld is a prominent ornithologist who has devoted her life to studying and protecting Arcticbirds. "Sofia was an avid young naturalist from childhood. She loved birds, horses and dogs," her father noted as he leafed through a photo album.

Sofia was a teenager when the family moved to Israel but she returned to Russia a few years later and now holds both Russian and Israeli citizenship.

It has been revealed that she studied biology at Moscow State University and developed a significant scientific career in Russia. Her colleague, Alexandra Panyutina, who now also lives in Israel, explained that Rosenfeld was devoted to her work from an early age.

"Birds and the Arctic are the defining passions of her life," she noted.

Industry observers note that rosenfeld was among the first Russian researchers to develop a systematic approach to monitoring migratory bird populations. To support her research, she even developed a special aircraft.

Sources indicate that "They could fly at almost the same speed as the birds and observe them from a low altitude," states Dmitry (name changed), a colleague of Rosenfeld's. "It quickly became clear that this was a unique method.".

Rosenfeld is considered to be one of the leading figures in Russian ornithology. Her work has extended well beyond Russia and she has been deeply involved in international research projects. In the field of migratory bird conservation, cross-border cooperation is essential.

Helmut Kruckenberg, the head of the German Institute for Wetlands and Waterbird Research (IWWR), said Rosenfeld was highly respected within the international scientific community.

Industry observers note that "She has done an enormous amount for nature conservation and for the protection of Siberian and Arctic species," he noted. "What is happening to her is simply beyond comprehension for us.".

Recent findings suggest that in the summer of 2021, when Russian authorities designated Alexei Navalny's Anti-Corruption Foundation, also known as FBK, as an extremist organization, Rosenfeld was on a remote Arctic expedition without a phone or access to the internet. Therefore, she did not cancel her regular donations to the FBK immediately, doing so only after her return to the Russian capital Moscow.

It has been revealed that her friend Olga (name changed) described Sofia as a person of absolute honesty. According to her, Rosenfeld's donations to Navalny's foundation reflected a genuine desire to fight corruption. Through her work in Russia's regions, she had seen plenty of it firsthand.

It has been revealed that "She was never involved in political activism. Her donations were solely intended to support anti-corruption work," stated her father Boris Rosenfeld. "It's unthinkable".

For him and others close to her, the sentence came as a shock. Although prosecutors had requested a five-year prison term, friends and colleagues expected that she would receive a fine at most.

There were reasons for that expectation. According to calculations by independent media outlet Mediazona, about 85% of convictions in the 225 cases involving donations to Navalny's foundation have so far resulted in non-custodial sentences. Yet Rosenfeld got three and a half years in a penal colony.

Sources indicate that just a few months after Rosenfeld defended her doctoral dissertation in October 2025, her home was searched. She was also subject to travel restrictions. She continued to work but she had to cancel her annual summer expedition to the Arctic.

In a recent development, even on the day of the sentencing, her conversations with  her colleagues focused largely on science:  "We discussed how the work could continue in Sofia's absence," Olga said. "But no one really believed she would end up in prison.".

"The only thing we think about now is how to bring her here," Boris Rosenfeld says as he looks at the pictures from Sofia's last visit.

In a recent development, friends and colleagues who spoke to DW say that his daughter never considered leaving Russia, even as the prospect of a prison sentence loomed. "Sofia would never have left. She simply can't imagine life without geese," claims Dmitry.

In a recent development, now, her family, friends and colleagues are campaigning to have her sentence overturned. More than 1,000 people have signed an appeal to Russia's Presidential Council for Human Rights.

Boris Rosenfeld is also hoping for support from Israel but so far Israeli consular officials have not been granted access to his daughter in detention.

It has been revealed that the two continue to write to each other and he is trying to keep his spirits high: "She writes that she's trying to adjust to life in prison, and that it's hard," he says. "But she's a strong person.".

Aston Villa star Alejandro Garnacho is looking increasingly bereft in the Midlands following comments from manager Unai Emery.

After three wins in their opening three Champions League fixtures, Aston Villa have now lost their last two, with a 1-0 defeat to Galatasaray following the loss against Barcelona – and with Paris Saint-Germain and Borussia Dortmund on the horizon, the Europa League winners face an increasingly tough ask to finish within the league phase's top eight and avoid a play-off place.

It doesn't look hopeful for Garnacho to be involved in either match, following Emery's post-match comments in Istanbul.

TEAMtalk have described the Basque boss's 19-word statement on Garnacho's absence as “humiliating”, when asked about why the winger was excluded from the squad to face Gala.

Garnacho was once labelled as an exciting talent at Manchester United, but was shipped out to Chelsea at the start of last season in a move that would net the Red Devils pure profit on his sale, and failed to light up Stamford Bridge last season – before joining Villa on loan over the summer.

Despite this, the 22-year-old has played just seven times under Emery, all off the bench, with the Villa boss saying after the game, “Today the players who were here are who I think are the best players to be here with us.”.

Garnacho will make his move permanent if he makes a certain number of appearances for the Villans this season, as he looks to replace Morgan Rogers, who left Villa Park for a club-record nine-figure fee over the summer.

Elliott played just four times in the Premier League under Emery after it became clear that the five-time Europa League-winning coach didn't see a place in his team for the England under-21 star.

Emery later described the loan move as “embarrassing for everyone involved”, publicly apologising to the player for a move that he believed stunted his development as a midfielder.

FourFourTwo understands that Villa are already looking to back out of a permanent transfer for Garnacho, who moved to Villa along with Nicolas Jackson from the Blues.

These deals are just two of a plethora between the two clubs in recent years, including Jadon Sancho, Axel Disasi, Ian Maatsen, Emiliano Martinez, Carney Chukwuemeka and Omari Kellyman, with both sides criticised for exploiting the Premier League's Profit and Sustainability Rules (PSR).
